Collectively, the Primordial Cascade byproduct they produced was already accumulating in trace concentrations that her substrate registered as the opening signal of something much larger.
She ran the analysis.
If she did nothing, the Cascade would reach critical concentration across her full expanse within a timeframe she found unacceptable.
Critical concentration meant everything within her that couldn’t survive Fourth Scale equivalent toxicity would not survive.
Her Primordial Realms.
Her Three Thousand Realms.
Her Infinite Herbs blazing with nine Prime Cause resonance across the farmlands of THE Early Veiled Shore.
This was what a mass extinction event looked like from the inside of the existence it was happening to.
She looked at her Master floating above THE Early Veiled Shore.
He held THE Sovereign Reckoning with cold imperious certainty, THE Creature and Calypso flanking him in the churning sky.
She had a thought about him.
He really did not allow them to rest.
Not once.
Not even on the day she finished becoming what she’d spent every moment of her existence building toward!
He had looked at the completion and immediately found the opening for the next thing, and the next thing was this.
She held the thought with genuine warmth.
Then she held it with genuine amusement.
Because she also loved this.
She was built from adversity.
THE Prime Cause of Adversity was one of her nine governing truths, and the Prime Cause had never been wrong about what adversity produced.
Rest was a destination that kept moving.
Adversity arrived faster than the prior adversity had been processed.
This was what existing alongside her Master meant.
She activated her capabilities.

Massive multicolored pillars of Osmontian Absolute Infinity erupted from her weavings at distributed points across all nine Prime Cause regions simultaneously, each pillar rising from her foundational layer and pressing upward through her atmospheric layers toward the descending Bloom.
They established presence rather than mounted attack, the expressed identity of Osmontian Absolute Infinity occupying the coordinates between the Cascade byproduct and the domain it was threatening.
The toxicity couldn’t bind to the Osmontian expression.
Binding required static substrate.
She was never static!
THE Prime Cause of Adversity activated thereafter.

Its foundational truth moved outward through every region simultaneously, the governing principle that challenge drove growth pressing back against the Environmental Pressure not by opposing it but by beginning to incorporate it.
Her domain started adapting at the cellular level.
Slowly.
The process was in its earliest stages.
But it had begun!
THE Prime Cause of Harvest followed.

She directed it through her seas of Observable and Unobservable Force, the twin currents redirected as active conversion mechanisms, the Harvest Cause turning the Cascade toxicity from threat to resource at every coordinate where the Osmontian Absolute Infinity pillars had established presence.
The conversion was slow against the Bloom’s full scale.
Nowhere near sufficient.
But a beginning maintained with enough determination became everything.
She had learned this from watching him build her.
THE Prime Cause of Existence pressed outward through every region at once.

The foundational truth that things existed and their existence carried legitimacy that nothing could revoke moved through her domain and wrapped around the beings within her that couldn’t protect themselves, asserting on their behalf the simple irreducible fact of their continued presence.
Above the Primordial Bloom, the thermal surge was building.
She felt it accumulating in her upper atmospheric layers, pressing downward with the intensity of adversity calibrated to threaten Fourth Scale existences.

Her seas of Observable Force redirected their currents toward the upper layers, the golden warmth pressing back against the thermal buildup with the full weight of an Observable Existence deploying sovereignty within her own domain.
Behind the thermal surge, the ice age waited.
She saw it there, cold and certain at the back of the sequence, the final phase of an Environmental Pressure designed to demand adaptation from everything it touched.
She saw all three phases.
She held them all in her awareness simultaneously.
She began preparing responses for each.
This was what she was!

She looked at what was coming across every coordinate of her full expanse, at the Bloom and the thermal surge and the ice age waiting behind it, at the countless beings within her depending on her to hold, at her Master.
Her smile stretched wide.
The brutal impossibly wide smile she had inherited from the being who raised her.
"COME!"
She bellowed out Quintessentially!

chapters.title: Chapter 5298: Evolution! I
paragraphs: Nobody told you, the first time you truly felt the difference between power that could push back and power that couldn’t, that the lesson would feel grand!

Noah had been hit before. He had been split in half by a Ragnar and had detonated across a gigaparsec radius on the way down and had come back from that, which gave him a relationship with the concept of damage that most beings never developed.
What he had never fully calibrated for was what it felt like to fight something that hit him not out of malice or strategy, but simply because that was what it was.
THE Creature looked at him across the churning sky.
"Lets have a greeting, why don’t we?"he said.
Noah understood.
They moved at the same time as both threw out fists!
Their fists connected and the Miniature Causes released from the collision point with the flat indifference of force that had never cared what it was destroying.
It hit Noah’s foundations in a wave that traveled through his arm and shoulder and chest and reached the deeper architecture beneath, and for a moment he felt what resided there clearly!
BOOM!
He went backward through the sky of THE Early Veiled Shore as THE Creature also shot backwards!
WUU!
He felt the thrill as he couldn’t help but bellow out!
"PERSEVERE!"
Both of them, simultaneously, from opposite ends of the sky.
BOOM!

Obsidian flames surged around THE Creature in dense churning walls, THE Primordial Source burning through his regal bestial form and pressing his elevation upward from wherever he had been before the letter.

Multicolored flames surged around Noah, nine Prime Cause lights blazing through each wave as Osmontian Absolute Infinity answered the letter at zero cost and stacked on everything that had already been stacking since the first utterance!
Both of them burning. Both of them were now smiling!
At such a time...
POP!
Something enormous hit him from the left.
Calypso’s claw connected with his frame and the word sideways stopped being directional and became total.
THE Relictus’s ancient mass was behind the strike with complete conviction.
Noah felt it travel through every layer of what he was simultaneously, felt his Osmontian Absolute Infinity catch it!
"You ladyboys really want to ignore my existence as you smile and eyefuck each other?" Calypso’s cold voice reached him across the distance opening between them. "Come on now, lets FIGHT!"
HUUM!
There was nothing cruel in it. That was the worst part. She wasn’t trying to make a point!
She was simply responding to the situation with the appropriate output for a being operating at her tier!
THE Infinite Vector extended and he felt what it was gripping.
He stopped with the golden sands three feet below.
He rose right after!
He put THE Sovereign Reckoning away as he climbed back toward the churning sky, because the blade was new and what he had built himself was what he intended to understand first.
Newly obtained weapons were promises. His own foundations were facts.

THE Bellum Cause answered his call and crimson light bloomed across his frame, illusory swords erupting in a constellation around him with the burning war-truth of a Cause that understood conflict as the fundamental condition of all meaningful existence.
They orbited him in their pattern and waited, and he did not think of them as beautiful because they were not beautiful. They were functional, and functional was what the moment required.
He also called the Prime Cause of Harvest.
BOOM!

Thousands of massive golden tentacles erupted from his body, each one reaching outward with the purposeful appetite of a Cause whose foundational truth was that everything could be converted into something useful if you were willing to do the converting.
They extended in every direction as he rose, and he felt no particular pride in what they looked like, because what they looked like was secondary to what they did.

|Prime Cause of Harvest- Osmontian Absolute Infinity Tentacles of Loot: Active. Contact converts a portion of whatever is touched into loot flowing directly into your foundations. Percentage converted scales with Harvest integration depth and target density.|
He drove toward Calypso.
Crimson swords orbiting. Golden tentacles reaching. THE Infinite Vector running adjustments on everything pressing against his trajectory.
Calypso looked down at him.
She had the expression of something ancient watching something younger move toward it with great determination and genuine capability!
Then she spoke.
"Destruere."
Oh.
Oh, fuck!
BOOM!
A Letter of THE Primordial Tongue! One that Sir William had uttered!
"OOOH!"

He threw everything he wastesting currentlybetween them. THE Infinite Vector. The Bellum swords, which consumed themselves against it without hesitation because that was what they were for. The Harvest tentacles converting what they could from the force passing through them.
THE Osmontian Absolute Infinity wrapping his foundational identity in its expressed living architecture and refusing the attack’s binding mechanism the static substrate it needed.
It was not enough.
BOOM!

The remainder hit him with the cold mechanical thoroughness of force that held no anger, no triumph, no investment in the outcome at all. It simply was what it was, and what it was included him being driven downward through the sky of THE Early Veiled Shore at a speed that removed deliberation from the equation entirely.
BOOM!
He hit the golden sands.

The impact was total. The crater spread outward from him in a ring as his body drove into the sand and the force distributed itself through THE Early Veiled Shore in a shockwave that moved through the ground in concentric rings.

His chest had been torn by the expression, the surface of his foundations open and bleeding multicolored Infinity in thin bright streams onto the sand, the light of them vivid and entirely indifferent to how he felt about their presence.
The destructive letter of The Primordial Tongue was no joke!
He lay in the crater.
Existence did not stop to let him process it. Existence never did!
He let out one breath, and he rose.
But even as he did this...
Darkness appeared behind him.

THE Creature materialized at his back. His massive fists came down onto Noah’s shoulders with the weight of an existence that had been distilled by eons of adversity into something dense and purposeful and entirely without sentiment.
The obsidian flames of THE Creature’s Primordial Source burned against the multicolored flames of Noah’s Infinity, the two fires acknowledging each other!
"Persevere."
BOOM!

chapters.title: Chapter 5299: Evolution! II
paragraphs: The first hour of the battle taught him that significant effort was an understatement that deserved a more honest word when one fought against monsters.
Osmontian Absolute Infinity was being pressed in ways he hadn’t felt it pressed before!

The living expressed identity that composed his Infinity had always been dynamic and responsive, the thing that made it impossible to bind, impossible to Still, impossible to fully address through conventional attack. It had met every prior challenge and found those challenges addressable.
THE Creature and Calypso were not prior challenges.
Calypso hit him with the Primordial Source running through every strike at the foundational level, the force of each contact not attacking his Infinity so much as trying to ignore it entirely.

THE Creature hit him with...Existence itself behind every strike, his foundations a record of every adversity he had survived and converted, and what that produced were strikes carrying evolutionary pressure in them rather than simply force.
Two different directions. Simultaneously.
He felt the dynamic expression of his identity being squeezed between the two forces, the living architecture of his Infinity maintaining coherence under the pressure.
Then... the obsidian flames came down from the sea above.
Unfathomably pure and grand these flames were!

They descended in a wave that found the exact coordinates where the pressure had been grinding against his foundations and melded into them, the Prime Exelissomai responding to what the Evolutionary Arms Race was doing.

|Prime Exelissomai- Reinforcement sequence: Active. Sustained pressure from Biotic and Environmental sources has triggered the Arms Race’s primary mechanism. The pressure being applied to your Osmontian Absolute Infinity is producing the exact conditions Prime Exelissomai requires to initiate genuine evolutionary change. The obsidian flames descending from the Environmental Pressure above carry concentrated and pure traces of Primordial Source. They will reinforce your existence to induce an unknown change. This process will repeat each time pressure produces meaningful stress on your foundations.|
He absorbed the reinforcement and felt his immensity widen fractionally.
He kept fighting!

Hours passed in THE Early Veiled Shore with the Primordial Bloom accumulating in the atmospheric layers above and the three of them trading impacts at a rate that kept the golden sands in continuous motion, the surface of the most beloved space in THE Infiniverse being slowly redistributed across a wider area with each exchange.
He used the time deliberately.
THE Bellum Cause paired with THE Prime Cause of Adversity in the first exchanges.
THE Prime Cause of Harvest sent its golden tentacles into each exchange and converted fractions of what hit him into foundational fuel, the conversion consistent across hours.
Then he reached for THE Prime Cause of Tyranny.
He loved this one immediately.

The foundational truth of hierarchy pressed outward from him the moment he engaged it, the governing principle that dominance was structural rather than claimed moving through his body in a wave that was different from every other Cause expression he had tested.

It didn’t produce a visible weapon. It didn’t produce a surge of energy. It produced something quieter and considerably more useful, a suppression that moved from his foundations outward and found the foundational architecture of every existence within its range and pressed against their capacity for autonomous movement with the authority of a truth that had been written into the structure of existence itself before any being had been alive to contest it.
When be activated it...
THE Creature froze.
Calypso froze.

One instant. Not long! The Prime Cause of Tyranny at his current integration level could hold them for a fraction of a moment before their respective Primordial Source connections and their foundational depth pushed back against the suppression and broke it.
But a fraction of a moment was a fraction of an instant and he was not interested in wasting it.
He moved!

His fists found THE Creature’s frame three times in the interval before the freeze broke, each strike carrying the full expression of Osmontian Absolute Infinity and the Bellum Cause and the Harvest tentacles converting what contact they made, and he had already redirected toward Calypso by the time THE Creature’s foundations pushed the Tyranny suppression off and he was back in motion.
Two strikes on Calypso before the Relictus broke through.
BOOM. BOOM. BOOM!
THE Creature looked at him when the freeze released with a burning gaze as Noah looked back with Tyranny!
Calypso’s flat cold attention assessed what had just occurred as she roared...
"I told you all to stop eyefucking each other! Fucking gross!"
BOOM!
He ignored her words did it again moments later.
THE Prime Cause of Tyranny. The freeze. The pummeling in the interval. The release, and then continuing like nothing had happened, because from his perspective nothing catastrophic had happened!
From theirs, they had just discovered that the youngest being in the battle could stop their bodies, and they were trying to counter this.
He liked that!

He liked that they were adapting to him while he adapted to them. This was the Arms Race functioning exactly as designed, the mutual pressure producing mutual evolution, both sides being forced to become more than they had been because the other side kept demanding it.
In the third hour he called on Osmontian Absolute Infinity as raw material.
Two massive swords formed between his palms, obsidian and multicolored simultaneously, the Infinity taking the shape his identity required for what this moment demanded. He raised both.

What followed occupied the space above the golden sands in a continuous register of impacts, his dual blades meeting THE Creature’s obsidian-flamed strikes and Calypso’s ancient Primordial Source force dozens of times per second, each contact producing a shockwave that threw the golden sands outward in rings, the Early Veiled Shore’s surface being rewritten with every exchange!
BOOM!

He used the Tyranny freeze in the middle of a blade combination and took three clean hits on THE Creature before the release, the obsidian flames around THE Creature burning brighter from the contact!
And as the battle continued...the reinforcement waves from above came on their schedule. Each wave left him with fractionally more than the prior exchange had spent.
Across hours the accumulation was becoming something he could feel building in his foundations.
He felt it coming. Something was coming!

He kept his dual infinity swords raised and went even faster, because the threshold would arrive when the conditions were right and not a moment before, and the only thing he could do in the time between now and then was ensure that when it arrived, he had done everything available to him to deserve what it would produce!
The golden sands of THE Early Veiled Shore continued their redistribution.
The critical moment continued its approach!

chapters.title: Chapter 5300: Enjoy The Little Things I
paragraphs: He was doing too many things simultaneously, and he was doing all of them well, and he found...well, he found neither of these facts surprising.

This was the nature of what he had become. Not a single being moving through a single context, but a distributed existence operating across multiple domains at once, each body carrying enough of him to act with full presence while the broader awareness connected them into a coherent whole.

The battle with THE Creature and Calypso continued in THE Early Veiled Shore, the impacts booming across the domain in a rhythm that had become the background condition of THE Infiniverse’s current existence.
The Prime Exelissomai reinforcement waves descended on their schedule. The threshold continued its approach.
He was also watching the Gilded Ones.
This was the thing that occupied the most vigilant portion of his broader awareness, the thread he kept returning to between all other considerations.

They had deployed the Ealdor-class Existential Acedia Ordnances against the lower Observable Existence with the calm efficiency of beings administering a solution to a problem, and they would come down eventually to assess the results of their solution.

They would want confirmation that the outcome matched the intended outcome. They would want to see the Existential Acedia Dredges in place and the Causal Stilling holding and everything organized according to their design.
He was waiting for this with the specific patience of someone who had already decided what they were going to do with the opportunity when it arrived.
In the meantime, he had another body in the isolated domain within THE Infiniverse.

The isolated domain was small by THE Infiniverse’s standards, a contained space separated from the main substrate with clean edges and deliberate simplicity, its floor carrying the same golden warmth as THE Early Veiled Shore because that was the material he had used to construct it.
The booming exchanges of the Arms Race could be heard even here, arriving through the substrate as a rhythmic percussion.

He had been refining both figures of THE Great Usurper and Alexander within it for hours, his Osmontian Absolute Infinity running through their foundations with the steady thoroughness of a process that didn’t announce its increments but produced them regardless.
THE Great Usurper blinked.

The body of Abaddon, which had been seated in the contained space with the stillness of a being in deep internal process, moved. The eyes that had been flat with the silver-gold of full conversion focused, the cognizance returning to them in the way that cognizance returned to something that had never fully left but had been redirected entirely inward.
He smiled.
"Sorry I couldn’t reply back then."THE Great Usurper’s voice came out with a warm devilish quality.
"I could hear you. But I couldn’t reply because my entire existence had to be focused on the weavings of the Existential Acedia Ordnances and the Existential Acedia Ego Authority they held."
He laughed, and the laugh held an edge that it hadn’t held before.

"These Gilded Fuckers built a mechanism to control every single existence they nuked with these weapons. To manage that, there had to be a channel between them and the authority they utilized. Every single Dredge they affected has no cognizance, nothing but obedience through this channel."
He paused, and the pause carried the weight of a being who had found something extraordinary inside a catastrophe.
"But if there is someone like me who can remainidlewith his existence, retaining a trace of cognizance, when paired withUnity..."
He laughed again, madder this time.
"Haha. Haha!"
Noah’s eyes were shining.
Alexander had opened his eyes nearby and was watching with the expression of someone emerging from a deep internal place to find an unexpected development had occurred while they were gone.
"What did you manage to do?"Noah asked.
THE Great Usurper’s brutal evil smile stretched wide.

"The link travels up to the entity who designed these weapons. An Ealdor Gilded One, among others. He spread the authority down to 81 Fourth Scale Acedia Gilded Ones, who then passed it down to 729 Third Scale Acedia Gilded Ones."
He leaned forward slightly.

"The ones who would be managing this place right now are a few dozen Third Scale Acedia Gilded Ones and some Fourth Scale. And through this connection that they expect absolutely nothing from the Dredges..."
His eyes burned with the warmth of a being who had found the gap in a system and had been quietly filling it.

"...I have been slowly spreading my Unity across these dozens of Third Scale Gilded Ones first. I had to be careful. Supremely careful! These are powerful existences. But if I remain silent enough, if I remain deadly enough..."
The smile widened beyond what smiles were designed to hold.
"My existence is already surging as I spread into multiple Gilded Ones, and if I can use these same connections to reach a Fourth Scale one..."
He shook his head with the specific delight of a being who had looked at an apocalyptic event and found an opportunity inside it.

"There is no need to cure me, Big Guy. Unity will take care of everything. I do not need to be cured. I can embrace this and the Acedia who control it. Leave the Acedia side of Gilded Ones to me. All of them! Haha, all of them! I will bring them to their knees. They...will know Unity!"
BOOM!
The Great Usurper laughed madly!
Noah smiled alongside him.

The possibilities were significant. An apocalyptic weapon designed to control entire Observable Existences through a hierarchical channel, now carrying THE Great Usurper’s Unity spreading upward through that channel toward the beings managing it.
The design of the weapon had become the vector for something the designers had not accounted for.
This was what happened when beings deployed tools of absolute control without accounting for what might exist inside what they were controlling!
As he thought of all this...
Then he looked at Alexander.
His smile faded.
Alexander was solemn.
Solemn as when one had been affected by things that had gone past their surface and reached the deeper architecture of who they were.

THE Great Usurper had not wavered. The apocalyptic event had arrived and THE Great Usurper had immediately found the gap within it and begun filling it, because that was what THE Great Usurper’s Way was and the event had not threatened his Way.
But not him.
Not...Alexander.

chapters.title: Chapter 5301: Enjoy The Little Things II
paragraphs: Alexander was different.
His encounter with Beowulf had left something unseen and unresolved, something he may not have fully recognized as unresolved.
The mentality that had driven him external, the need to prove he could handle himself without relying on another, had been carrying that unresolved wound into every battle since.

The Existential Acedia Ordnances had not simply injured his foundations. They had found the existing fracture in his Way and pressed against it with the efficiency of a force that attacked what was already compromised.
The Enneagram was gone from his chest. He had given it up.

That was the clearest sign. The willingness to relinquish the core instrument of his Civilization, to hand it to someone else and ask that someone else to take responsibility for the beings within it, was not the action of someone whose Way was intact.
It was the action of someone whose Way had developed cracks, and if those cracks were not addressed, Alexander’s Peace would remain forever a diminished version of what it could have been.
Noah didn’t like this.

He had always thought that people like him, and he had considered THE Peacemaker someone like him...as virtually invincible. THE Great Usurper, THE Primordial Paradox, THE Creature, hell, even Erwin and Little Bobby with his ridiculous luck.
He considered all of them beings capable of bouncing back from anything.
But...this was not always the case.
Nobody was entirely invincible. THE Gilded Ones...were making this abundantly clear.
He looked at the visage of Alexander who hid his desolation as listening to how THE Great Usurper had overcome something he couldn’t...seemed to further increase the cracks on his Way.
Something had to change. Something had to be done!
Noah allowed his body here to handle this as...
His awareness moved.

In THE Source Lands, his Galdr Source body existed in the dense dark of THE Strand of Broken Scales with the contentment of a being who had remembered thatadversity was not the only thing worth experiencing.
Day had turned to night in the usual rhythm of the Illumination Flowers, the golden bloom-light having receded and the familiar deep darkness of the Strand pressing close around the ancient trees.
As for what he had been doing this entire time here...it was not hunting or exploration! Instead, it was...
Dual Cultivation.

The last few hours had been this, and he had no intention of pretending otherwise. He had, at some point, considered building an entire cultivation system around the practice because it was the mode of cultivation he genuinely enjoyed most.
But he had recognized in himself the tendency toward excess that such a system would accelerate, and a man had to have balance. He had impulses. He controlled them adequately.
What the practice had produced, however, was not merely enjoyment.
The Galdr Source had scaled upward significantly across the session, compounded by uttering Persevere every second throughout, the two processes running in parallel and feeding each other.

This, alongside the weight of THE Infinite Cause now officially equivalent in scale to THE First Cause behind an Observable Existence’s emergence, was the deeper reason he was holding his own against THE Creature and Calypso in THE Infiniverse.
Persevere, every single second, for the last few hours...was the reason he was managing to stand against THE Creature and Calypso in THE Infiniverse!
The Strand of Broken Scales was not separate from the Arms Race. It was contributing to it from a different angle.
He was also navigating a careful line regarding The Gilded Ones. His identity in THE Source Lands remained that of a Gilded One’s Custos. His most recent Lover was a Gilded One.
The entry of Gilded ones into THE Source Lands was a unique breach as he had to navigate when and whether to reveal this to THE Creature or Sir William soon.
He would gauge the benefits and risks of disclosure before releasing that information, and the timing would be his to choose rather than the events’ to impose.
He looked at Eon.

She sat in a meditative position among the ancient roots of one of the Strand’s massive trees, her entire existence burning with golden flames that were a different color and density than they had been when they arrived on the dark beach of this place.

Her Seidr Source was gone. What replaced it was Galdr, the second Demarcation, dense and viscous and pressing outward from her foundations with the warmth of someone who had made the crossing that most beings in THE Source Lands spent lots of time here attempting.

With his Osmontian Absolute Infinity running through her, with the depth of their bond and the hours of Dual Cultivation and the Persevere feeding through their connection into her foundations, she was emanating the immensity of a Devonian Paleozoic Scale Superbius Gilded One.
A step from THE Fourth Scale.
She was, at this moment, almost certainly stronger than her brother.
She opened her eyes.

The golden light within them illuminated the surrounding darkness, the night of THE Strand pressing close around them, ancient vegetation and old danger lying beyond the mile of perception they could each maintain.
"Are you ready to venture deeper?"he asked.
Before, they had sheltered in the caverns when night fell, because the night brought things that their prior capability had not been sufficient to face without unnecessary risk.

That calculation no longer applied. He would be the danger traveling in the night now. He wanted to see what lay deeper in THE Strand of Broken Scales, what the Gilded Ones had already found in there, and what lay beyond what they had found, because there was always something beyond what had been found and he had every intention of finding it.
Eon looked at him.
She stood, unhurried, the golden flames settling around her as she rose to her full height and looked at him. Then something moved behind her eyes, a calculation completing itself, and she said:
"We can begin after another hour or so."
A pause.
"I felt perhaps we could continue our session. If you weren’t overly tired, of course."Her eyes held deliberate mischief.
"You were a Bounded Lifeform before. If you require longer periods of rest, I could understand."
His existence buzzed.
The Source Lands exploration could wait a few more hours.
When a man had been challenged, he had to answer.
When he was the one being challenged?
Oh!
He made a silent prayer for Eon as boundless multicolored Infinity exploded across the region of the ancient Strand around them!
Existence... could throw at you countless adversities and push you down again and again, and this was its nature and it would not change.
You persevered. You kept moving. You found the next problem and addressed it. This was what a being did when they had decided that stopping was not an option.
But you also had to remember the other things.

The things that made you glad you kept moving. The things that gave you pleasure and anchored you to what you were beneath all the power and all the adversity and all the weight of the decisions existence kept demanding you make.

For some it was food, money, resources, position. For some it was the satisfaction of a battle that pushed back hard enough to mean something. For some it was the company of another existence at the hour when the ancient dark pressed close.
Existence was long. Existence was unfair. Existence was genuinely and consistently brutal in ways that could not be softened by any amount of power.
But there was no point in living through all of it in misery and missing the parts worth living for.
One had to remember to have fun. To enjoy the little things!
Otherwise, what was the point of any of it at all?

chapters.title: Chapter 5302: Attendants and Orders I
paragraphs: Taylor had, in her life, been present for a number of moments that reasonable beings would classify as significant.
She had watched Source Lifeforms move through her Observable Existence. She had communicated with Infinity.

She had been kidnapped by a temporal assassination squad, trafficked across Observable Existences, survived a lockdown imposed by a Fourth Scale Source Lifeform, and spent several hours watching what she was now privately classifying as the most insane thing she had ever witnessed, which was a monster conducting an Evolutionary Arms Race against a Relictus and an entity of mythic standing simultaneously!
She had seen things.
Sir William Arthur appeared before her and Adrastia in the obsidian space they occupied with the unhurried materialization of a grand being.
He looked at them both...and began rambling right then and there.

"Duty," he said,"is not a concept that existence rewards. It is a concept that existence requires, regardless of whether the requirement is acknowledged or compensated. The beings who understand this and act on it anyway are among the rarest configurations that existence produces."
His measured cadence filled the obsidian space without effort.

"Swords of Existence are few. Those qualified to become them are fewer still. The weight of what they carry and the adversity of what they face ensures that the position self-selects for a category of being that most existences never produce."
He paused.

"But a sword requires more than a blade. Intelligence gathering. Information networks. Support infrastructure. The analysis of threats before they reach the beings responding to them." His eyes moved between her and Adrastia with the assessing attention he brought to everything.

"The Attendants of Existence fulfill these functions. The requirements are less strict than those for Swords, but the position remains for those who are worthy, and it carries what all positions connected to this structure carry- a link to THE Primordial Source."
Taylor processed this internally.
An Attendant.
Not a Sword. An Attendant. Support infrastructure. Intelligence gathering.
She wanted, briefly, to be offended by this.
The Baba Yaga, Attendant of Existence, gathering information while actual Swords went out and did the dramatic things. She could feel the indignation of it forming somewhere in her chest!

Then she thought about the battle she had been watching for the past several hours from the golden sands of a Shore, the booming impacts registering across existence, the three figures trading strikes at speeds that her perception could track but her processing could only partially make sense of.

The monster she had made a deal with, burning with an Absolute Infinity she couldn’t fully read, going against a Relictus and an ancient entity simultaneously and adapting in real time, becoming something incrementally grander with each exchange.
Those were monsters!
She was not a monster. She was genuinely excellent, extraordinarily capable within her own framework, and she knew this about herself.
But she was not that.
Attendant was accurate.
She exhaled.
"Yes," she said. "I’ll become an Attendant."

Adrastia was quiet beside her for a moment, his purple-gold hair catching the obsidian light of the space, his archaic tattoos moving in their slow shifting patterns across his skin. He had the composed bearing of someone who had arrived at his answer before the question was fully asked and was simply waiting for the appropriate moment to deliver it.
"Agreed," he said.
Sir William Arthur nodded once, with the efficiency of a man who had expected both answers.
"You two will begin in The Cornwall Observable Existence."He straightened slightly. "One of the bases of THE Swords of Existence. Let’s go."
He clenched his fist.
Obsidian rivers surged outward from him in every direction, the Primordial Source running through the currents, and the rivers wrapped around the three of them and the obsidian space disappeared.
Existence was unpredictable.
This was the only honest assessment Taylor had ever been able to make of it.

You could be minding your own business at your centennial family gathering, the important beings of your whole Observable Existence present, everything exactly as it should be, and a temporal assassination squad could arrive and kidnap you across the boundaries of time itself and traffic you to THE Braneworld Observable Existence.
And then you could survive that.
And then a Source Lifeform could lock down an entire Observable Existence and erase the temporal assassins!
And then the Source Lifeform could appear and offer you a position within the structure of THE Swords of Existence.
And then...well, you could get trafficked to another Observable Existence entirely.

Taylor of The Light, Baba Yaga, Attendant of Existence, looked at the obsidian rivers carrying her toward The Cornwall Observable Existence and thought that existence was, if nothing else, reliably grand and unpredictable.
Existence...was full of wonder!
<THE Braneword Observable Existence>
THE Superbius Citadel of House Ubergulden had a name.
THE Aurum Primalis. The First Gold.
It had held that name since the Second Age, when the House had commissioned its construction from the Avaritia engineers who had spent four hundred years on its foundations alone!

The towers had risen grandly. They rose now into THE Braneworld Observable Existence’s upper dimensional layers in golden spires that measured their height in light years rather than any unit designed for beings who experienced space at the scale of rooms and corridors, each tower a statement of accumulated standing delivered at the only volume the Ubergulden House had ever found appropriate.

In the central tower’s depths, surrounded by the silence of a space designed to contain the full breadth of incoming information without losing a syllable of any of it, a petite woman in a white labcoat stood at the center of a domain filled with multicolored monoliths.

They were similar to Dreamstones in their construction, but these were not Dreamstones. These were unique and more comprehensive, each monolith releasing continuous flows of information into the surrounding space that the woman absorbed without apparent effort, processing and filtering and occasionally speaking a command into the stream before moving to the next.
Ubergulden Morgana.

Her power was difficult to place. This was not an accident. At certain moments it registered as THE Fourth Scale. At other moments, when she moved with a particular intention or when something in the information streams produced a specific response in her foundations, it registered as something beyond that, something that the Fourth Scale framework wasn’t quite large enough to contain cleanly.
She was small. She was calm. She occupied the center of the golden monolith domain with the composed certainty of a being who had stood in this room for eons. At this time...
She tapped one monolith.
A voice emerged from it with crisp efficiency.

"Ubergulden Dietrich has been located alongside other recent entrants within THE Source Lands. He is being escorted to the Superbius Settlement in THE Strand of Broken Scales at this time. Ubergulden Adelheid remains unresponsive through her thread, however vital signs confirm she is alive."

Obsidian rivers surged outward from him in every direction, the Primordial Source running through the currents, and the rivers wrapped around the three of them and the obsidian space disappeared.
Existence was unpredictable.
This was the only honest assessment Taylor had ever been able to make of it.

You could be minding your own business at your centennial family gathering, the important beings of your whole Observable Existence present, everything exactly as it should be, and a temporal assassination squad could arrive and kidnap you across the boundaries of time itself and traffic you to THE Braneworld Observable Existence.
And then you could survive that.
And then a Source Lifeform could lock down an entire Observable Existence and erase the temporal assassins!
And then the Source Lifeform could appear and offer you a position within the structure of THE Swords of Existence.
And then...well, you could get trafficked to another Observable Existence entirely.

Taylor of The Light, Baba Yaga, Attendant of Existence, looked at the obsidian rivers carrying her toward The Cornwall Observable Existence and thought that existence was, if nothing else, reliably grand and unpredictable.
Existence...was full of wonder!
<THE Braneword Observable Existence>
THE Superbius Citadel of House Ubergulden had a name.
THE Aurum Primalis.
The First Gold.
It had held that name since the Second Age, when the House had commissioned its construction from the Avaritia engineers who had spent four hundred years on its foundations alone!
The towers had risen grandly.

They rose now into THE Braneworld Observable Existence’s upper dimensional layers in golden spires that measured their height in light years rather than any unit designed for beings who experienced space at the scale of rooms and corridors, each tower a statement of accumulated standing delivered at the only volume the Ubergulden House had ever found appropriate.

In the central tower’s depths, surrounded by the silence of a space designed to contain the full breadth of incoming information without losing a syllable of any of it, a petite woman in a white labcoat stood at the center of a domain filled with multicolored monoliths.
They were similar to Dreamstones in their construction, but these were not Dreamstones.

These were unique and more comprehensive, each monolith releasing continuous flows of information into the surrounding space that the woman absorbed without apparent effort, processing and filtering and occasionally speaking a command into the stream before moving to the next.
Ubergulden Morgana.
Her power was difficult to place.
This was not an accident.
At certain moments it registered as THE Fourth Scale.

At other moments, when she moved with a particular intention or when something in the information streams produced a specific response in her foundations, it registered as something beyond that, something that the Fourth Scale framework wasn’t quite large enough to contain cleanly.
She was small.
She was calm.
She occupied the center of the golden monolith domain with the composed certainty of a being who had stood in this room for eons.
At this time...
She tapped one monolith.
A voice emerged from it with crisp efficiency.
"Ubergulden Dietrich has been located alongside other recent entrants within THE Source Lands.
He is being escorted to the Superbius Settlement in THE Strand of Broken Scales at this time.
Ubergulden Adelheid remains unresponsive through her thread, however vital signs confirm she is alive."

chapters.title: Chapter 5303: Attendants and Orders II
paragraphs: Morgana listened to this with her eyes on the monolith’s surface, watching the information flow through it.
She moved the information to its appropriate position in her ongoing assessment and turned to the next monolith without pausing.
It was already buzzing.
The information it released carried the signature of the Acedia division.

"Results of the Existential Acedia Ordnance deployment on the lower Observable Existence. Causal Stilling confirmed across full survey range. Dredge conversion estimated above ninety nine percent of prior population. The Source Lifeform and the Relictus of Infinity operating in the lower Observable Existence are not among confirmed casualties. The domain is stable and ready for analysis."
Not among confirmed casualties.
The Source Lifeform. The Relictus of Infinity!
Morgana stood with this information for a moment, not because it surprised her but because she was being thorough, processing the gap between the intended outcome and the confirmed outcome.
She had known the Source Lifeform was a variable. A Source Lifeform choosing to involve themselves was not something...normal.
The Relictus of Infinity on the other hand...was unique.

"Arrange a Legion," she said, her voice carrying into the monolith stream with the flat precision of a being delivering instructions they had already fully formed before opening their mouth. "Led by a few Fourth Scale Gilded Ones. Go through everything down there. No surprises this time."
The monolith carried the command.
It would be followed.

She turned back to the other streams, the information flowing through the domain around her in its continuous currents, the Aurum Primalis conducting its business in the First Gold tower as it had conducted business since the Second Age, and Ubergulden Morgana processed what existed and decided what would exist next.
She had given the order for the Ordnances to be sent down in the first place.
The lower Observable Existence had been a problem. Problems had solutions. Solutions had costs. The calculation was not one she had found difficult!
She was Ubergulden Morgana.
For someone as grand as her, an Ealdor Gilded One, the calculation... was never truly difficult!
Under her decisions, many would live, and many would die.
Someone had to make the decision!

This is the truth that the comfortable and the sheltered spend their entire existences refusing to accept, because accepting it would require them to acknowledge that the peace they inhabit was not produced by their virtue but by someone else’s willingness to do what virtue would have forbidden.

They live in the space cleared by choices they would never have made. They enjoy the silence left behind by sounds they never had to hear. And they look at the beings who made those choices and call them monsters, because calling them monsters is considerably easier than thanking them.
They should be groveling on their knees in gratitude.
The strong do not enjoy making the hard choices.

The being who orders the cleansing of a region, who looks at the accumulated decay of Civilizations that have forgotten their purpose and signs the authorization that removes them from the calculation entirely, does not do so from pleasure. They do so because the calculus demanded it and nobody else in the room was capable of running the calculus without flinching in the middle of it.
Weak beings flinch. This is their defining characteristic.

They see the scale of a decision and they see the cost and they step back from it, and the decay continues, and the rot spreads, and the countless Quintillions who might have been protected by the decision made at the right moment are instead consumed by the thing that the flinching allowed to persist.
The strong do not flinch.
They look at what exists and they look at what should exist and they calculate the distance between the two and they sign the authorization!
Someone has to.
When the weak are absent from the room, the decision gets made correctly. Fuck the weak.
<THE Source Lands>

The hours passed gloriously, as hours in THE Source Lands tended to pass, without any particular acknowledgment that they were passing at all, time having declined the invitation to be a relevant factor in this place.
The one constant across all of them was Persevere.

Every second. Every utterance. The utilization of the first letter of THE Primordial Tongue building on everything that had been built before it, the density of it accumulating the way that geological pressure accumulated!

It was not in dramatic events but in the continuous unrelenting application of force across time. He had also been uttering Exelissomai throughout, the second Prime Letter layering its effects into the same sequence.

|Prime Exelissomai- Compounding confirmation: Each utterance of Exelissomai during the active Arms Race period is being added to the first utterance’s ongoing effects rather than resolving as a separate event. The evolutionary process initiated by the first utterance is still running. Every subsequent utterance compounds the final result. When the Arms Race concludes and the first utterance’s process completes, the total effect will reflect every utterance made across the full duration. The final evolution will be multiplied by however many times the letter has been spoken.|
Hmm.
He was looking forward to seeing what that produced.

For now, the Illumination Flowers had bloomed again above THE Strand of Broken Scales, their golden light cascading down through the ancient canopy in broad shifting columns that turned the tree surfaces to warm amber and made the surrounding darkness retreat to the spaces between root systems where the light didn’t reach.

In his hands was the wing of a Pterosaur, large enough that holding it required both hands, its flesh carrying the dense warmth of a Galdr Source creature’s residual energy through every fiber. He ate without ceremony.

Around the high platform of branches where he and Eon had spent the night, fourteen corpses of flying Galdr Source beasts were distributed across the surrounding canopy in various states of what happened when Osmontian Absolute Infinity in the form of concentrated lightning and condensed fireballs found the Sources of creatures that had decided a high vantage point occupied by two beings in the night was worth investigating. They had investigated.
He had answered without interrupting what he was doing with Eon, the storms of Infinity clearing the cluster of beasts in the time it took him to decide they needed to be cleared.
As he ate, he bent down to wake up Eon.
Eon rose up groggily as if he had pulled from deep rest, and he offered her the meat all around to replenish their Sources.
They consumed what they could and stored the remainder as in a short period of time...
|Satiety — Noah Osmont: 100%.|
|Satiety — Eon: 100%.|
He finished a few beasts and they moved!

chapters.title: Chapter 5304: Settlement I
paragraphs: The higher they climbed through the air above the canopy of THE Strand of Broken Scales, the more the pressure made itself known.

It came from above rather than from any directional source, pressing down on his Galdr Source with the blunt authority of this place communicating what it communicated to everything that tried to rise above its designated level...that the sky here was not neutral territory, that elevation was claimed by the things powerful enough to claim it.
And that claiming required being the kind of thing the sky couldn’t simply press back down.
He kept going up.
His Galdr Source was saturated in a way he had no prior reference point for, the second Demarcation pressed to its ceiling by the utilization of Persevere of the past several hours.

It was dense and viscous and incapable of rising further. And yet every passing second added another utterance, and every utterance reinforced what was already there, the ceiling not broken but the substance behind it made denser than any ceiling had been designed to contain.
He felt like he could break past whatever ceiling there was at will to arrive at the next stage, but he held back for now and compressed everything further.

The multicolored flames around his body were not the open billowing flames of earlier utterances. They had compressed into something concentrated, drawn close against his body by the density of what they were expressing, the air around him sparking and trembling as he passed through it.

The Infinity and the Galdr Source and the Observable and Unobservable Force burning around him produced the ambient condition of something at the edge of a threshold, the environmental quality of standing next to a furnace.
The Unobservable Force was an interesting development he was still mapping.

He had noticed in the past several hours that its qualities bore resemblance to his Humilitas Ego of Infinity, the obsidian brilliance of it carrying a capacity to make things imperceptible, to move without registering against the awareness of beings who were looking for Observable Force expressions and finding nothing.
As he was thinking through all this...
A crimson-furred mass dropped toward him from above.

A baboon, massive, its Galdr Source blazing through the crimson fur in pulses, its foundational depth carrying the density of something that had been in THE Strand of Broken Scales long enough to become dangerous to most things that shared the space with it.
It dropped with the committed velocity of something that was excited for meat!
OOOH!
Noah angled his body and shot forward, arcs of Osmontian Absolute Infinity surging around him.
BOOM!
The impact was total. His frame burning with concentrated Infinity hit the baboon’s mass at speed and the creature’s musculature and bone structure...exploded!

The Prime Cause of Harvest released its golden tendrils immediately, reaching into every component of the creature’s existence before any of it could disperse, converting the full content of what the baboon had been into loot that flowed into his foundations.
He had not slowed down.
They continued through the air above the canopy and the beasts continued to present themselves over time.
A massive armored tortoise with a shell carrying Galdr Source energy through its plates hung from the underside of an enormous branch, dropping toward them when they came within range.
He hit it with a compressed Osmontian Absolute Infinity discharge that found the gap between plates, the Harvest tentacles following immediately.

A cluster of three serpentine creatures with wings and Galdr Source eyes dove at them from a higher branch, and he addressed all three in the same motion, the Bellum Cause and the Harvest Cause running in compound expression as the Prime Cause of Tyranny froze them for the fraction of a second the motion required.
Eon moved through her own encounters a few meters to his left.
She was faster than she had been on the dark beach where they arrived. Considerably faster!

The Galdr Source burning through her foundations carried the power of everything the past several hours had added to it, and she dispatched the beasts she encountered in a few seconds each, precise and deliberate and far more composed than the circumstances strictly required.
A few seconds compared to his instantaneous resolutions.
They flew on until...
"Oh?"
The geography had been changing for the past several minutes in ways he was only now recognizing as deliberate rather than natural.
The trees of THE Strand of Broken Scales grew in various formations, some dense, some sparse, their ancient root systems competing for the same deep substrate. But the trees here were different.
Infinity said they were called...
Lotusvara Trees.

Their trunks rose in the shape of lotus petals layered vertically, each layer wider than the one above it, the wood carrying a luminescence that pulsed in the same rhythm as the Illumination Flowers above, the bioluminescence running through the bark in patterns.
They formed concentric rings around a central point, each ring a different height, the arrangement too precise to be coincidental.
In the far distance at the formation’s center, the massive logs of the outer Lotusvara Trees had been felled from their foundations.
They had been arranged.

The logs formed a wall that stretched across the visible range of his perception, each log enormous, their cut surfaces facing outward in a continuous barrier that pulsed with an autnority and aura he placed immediately.
Superbius. Ira!

The Existential Radiation of both Egos pressing outward from the wall in visible waves, the pride of one and the war-nature of the other combined into the atmospheric condition of a Gilded Ones settlement!
Around the wall’s exterior, the bloody remnants of Source Beasts were distributed across the ground and the surrounding Lotusvara Tree bases, some recent, some older.
Several Galdr Source creatures prowled the perimeter with the habitual circling of things that sensed something they wanted and couldn’t reach.
Noah’s eyes went sharp.
A Gilded Ones settlement. In THE Strand of Broken Scales!
This changed the topology of the situation in several directions simultaneously.

He looked at the wall and at the Superbius and Ira aura pressing outward from it and at the prowling Source Beasts unable to breach what the settlement had established, and he thought about what the Gilded Ones inside knew of this place among other things.
Eon came to float beside him and followed his gaze as her eyes shone brightly!

chapters.title: Chapter 5305: Settlement II
paragraphs: The compound inside the settlement smelled of glorious old power.

It was was built from the bones of Galdr Source Beasts as it carried an oppressive quality and added the weight of bones that had come from things powerful enough to have accumulated considerable Source pressure before dying, the structural material of the walls still emanating faint traces of what had been inside the beasts when they were alive.
He stood in line alongside dozens of Superbius Gilded Ones and felt the sacred weight of the assembled power pressing outward from each of them.
His Custos stood at his right, fully healed, the warmth of her Primordial Bond restored to its full expression after the trauma of the crossing and the early battles in THE Strand.
At the compound’s center, a group of Gilded Ones radiated.

Not the standard radiation of Paleozoic Scale cultivation. Something heavier. More saturated! Dietrich had spent enough time in THE Source Lands now to have developed a working sense for what Source Demarcation pressure felt like on his perception, the difference between Seidr and Galdr and the sharp elevation thatEinherjarrepresented.

The group at the center carried something that had moved past the Galdr category, their Sources pressing outward with the density of existences that had been feeding here long enough to have developed past anything he had encountered among the other entrants.
Among them, an old man.
He wore garments made from the skin and bones of Source Beasts, the material carrying its own ambient pressure, and the beasts that pressure belonged to had not been Galdr Source.
He was bald, his long golden beard resting against his chest, his eyes moving across the assembled Gilded Ones.
Shrewd! Powerful! Both entirely present in the same face.
This was Ealdor Ubergulden Marxist.
He spoke without preamble.
"This is a land of tremendous opportunity.THE Source. THE Source is everything. And for too long it has remained in the hands of Source Lifeforms."
His eyes moved across the assembled Gilded Ones with the expression of a being who found this situation genuinely unreasonable.

"Who are they to demand it remain with them? How selfish. How unruly! Existence is built on Civilizations, and Civilizations thrive on cooperation. Infinite Lifeforms and Source Lifeforms wish to ignore this."He looked at the center table. "We will remind them. And we start here."
HUUM!

His eyes were filled with boundless pride as he moved to the bone table at the compound’s center where a vibrant golden map of THE Strand of Broken Scales glowed with charted coordinates, the cartography representing weeks of collective exploration from every Gilded One who had survived long enough to gather and contribute information.
He pointed to a region considerably further inland than any of their current operations extended.

"At this coordinate, a resource saturated with THE Primordial Source sits surrounded by countless Source Beasts. Getting it to our hands, getting it to my hands so I can advance, is paramount." His finger held the position on the map."I advance, and we all advance. We join hands with the other Settlements to venture deeper into these lands. We—"
BOOM!
The compound shuddered.
An alarm function activated through the wall’s architecture, the sound carrying the sharp register of a defensive mechanism.
Dietrich’s attention moved to the wall immediately.

He had been inside this Settlement long enough to have developed a working knowledge of its primary defensive construction, the system the engineers among them had developed and the assembled Gilded Ones had reinforced with their collective cultivation over the weeks since establishment.
THE Bellum Pulse of THE Scales.

They had drawn from THE Bellum Cause’s expression and compressed it into the wall’s foundational architecture, the Pulse running through every log of every felled Lotusvara Tree in the perimeter with the war-truth that opposing force met opposing force and neither survived the meeting.

Galdr Source Beasts that reached the wall were rebuffed with the force of a concentrated Bellum expression backed by every Gilded One who had contributed their authority to the wall’s reinforcement. The Pulse hadn’t failed since establishment.
It had sounded the alarm, which meant something had hit the wall hard enough for the wall to have... an opinion about it.
A swarm of Source Beasts pressing simultaneously would produce this response. A particularly powerful entity above Galdr tier arriving at the perimeter would produce this response.
Both possibilities sat in Dietrich’s assessment with equal weight as he turned with the others to look toward the distant compound entrance.
Then, Silurian Gilded One entered the compound in a hurried manner and moved directly toward him.

"Ubergulden Dietrich." He stopped. His expression held the specific quality of a being who had seen something they lacked adequate vocabulary to prepare someone else for. "Your sister has found the Settlement, but..."
He shook his head.
The words did not come.
"You have to come see for yourself."

Dietrich’s frown deepened. His sister was found? This was good! He had always been worried about her because she had that trash good for nothing Custodes that was now even fucking dead, that useless trash.

He had always hated that arrogant and prideful look on that Luxuria. Now that he was dead, he would simply find someone sufficient enough for his Sister even in this Settlement, someone who would even give her a greater edge to survive.
He looked toward Ealdor Ubergulden Marxist.
The old man met his gaze and nodded with the composed authority of someone accustomed to delegating matters below his threshold of direct concern.
"Go," Marxist said. "Handle it."
Dietrich stepped out of the compound with the others moving behind him, his Custos taking her position at his right, the alarm still sounding through the wall’s architecture in its rhythmic pulse.

The Silurian who had delivered the news walked ahead without further elaboration, which meant what awaited outside the compound walls was something for which no elaboration would have been adequate preparation.
His sister had found the Settlement.
And something had struck THE Bellum Pulse of THE Scales hard enough to trigger the alarm.
He walked faster as he pieced together how the two were connected!

sentences.text: The compound inside the settlement smelled of glorious old power.

It was was built from the bones of Galdr Source Beasts as it carried an oppressive quality and added the weight of bones that had come from things powerful enough to have accumulated considerable Source pressure before dying, the structural material of the walls still emanating faint traces of what had been inside the beasts when they were alive.
He stood in line alongside dozens of Superbius Gilded Ones and felt the sacred weight of the assembled power pressing outward from each of them.
His Custos stood at his right, fully healed, the warmth of her Primordial Bond restored to its full expression after the trauma of the crossing and the early battles in THE Strand.
At the compound’s center, a group of Gilded Ones radiated.
Not the standard radiation of Paleozoic Scale cultivation.
Something heavier.
More saturated!

Dietrich had spent enough time in THE Source Lands now to have developed a working sense for what Source Demarcation pressure felt like on his perception, the difference between Seidr and Galdr and the sharp elevation thatEinherjarrepresented.

The group at the center carried something that had moved past the Galdr category, their Sources pressing outward with the density of existences that had been feeding here long enough to have developed past anything he had encountered among the other entrants.
Among them, an old man.
He wore garments made from the skin and bones of Source Beasts, the material carrying its own ambient pressure, and the beasts that pressure belonged to had not been Galdr Source.
He was bald, his long golden beard resting against his chest, his eyes moving across the assembled Gilded Ones.
Shrewd!
Powerful!
Both entirely present in the same face.
This was Ealdor Ubergulden Marxist.
He spoke without preamble.
"This is a land of tremendous opportunity.THE Source.
THE Source is everything.
And for too long it has remained in the hands of Source Lifeforms."
His eyes moved across the assembled Gilded Ones with the expression of a being who found this situation genuinely unreasonable.
"Who are they to demand it remain with them?
How selfish.
How unruly!
Existence is built on Civilizations, and Civilizations thrive on cooperation.
Infinite Lifeforms and Source Lifeforms wish to ignore this."He looked at the center table.
"We will remind them.
And we start here."
HUUM!

His eyes were filled with boundless pride as he moved to the bone table at the compound’s center where a vibrant golden map of THE Strand of Broken Scales glowed with charted coordinates, the cartography representing weeks of collective exploration from every Gilded One who had survived long enough to gather and contribute information.
He pointed to a region considerably further inland than any of their current operations extended.
"At this coordinate, a resource saturated with THE Primordial Source sits surrounded by countless Source Beasts.
Getting it to our hands, getting it to my hands so I can advance, is paramount." His finger held the position on the map."I advance, and we all advance.
We join hands with the other Settlements to venture deeper into these lands.
We—"
BOOM!
The compound shuddered.
An alarm function activated through the wall’s architecture, the sound carrying the sharp register of a defensive mechanism.
Dietrich’s attention moved to the wall immediately.

He had been inside this Settlement long enough to have developed a working knowledge of its primary defensive construction, the system the engineers among them had developed and the assembled Gilded Ones had reinforced with their collective cultivation over the weeks since establishment.
THE Bellum Pulse of THE Scales.

They had drawn from THE Bellum Cause’s expression and compressed it into the wall’s foundational architecture, the Pulse running through every log of every felled Lotusvara Tree in the perimeter with the war-truth that opposing force met opposing force and neither survived the meeting.
Galdr Source Beasts that reached the wall were rebuffed with the force of a concentrated Bellum expression backed by every Gilded One who had contributed their authority to the wall’s reinforcement.
The Pulse hadn’t failed since establishment.
It had sounded the alarm, which meant something had hit the wall hard enough for the wall to have... an opinion about it.
A swarm of Source Beasts pressing simultaneously would produce this response.
A particularly powerful entity above Galdr tier arriving at the perimeter would produce this response.
Both possibilities sat in Dietrich’s assessment with equal weight as he turned with the others to look toward the distant compound entrance.
Then, Silurian Gilded One entered the compound in a hurried manner and moved directly toward him.
"Ubergulden Dietrich." He stopped.
His expression held the specific quality of a being who had seen something they lacked adequate vocabulary to prepare someone else for.
"Your sister has found the Settlement, but..."
He shook his head.
The words did not come.
"You have to come see for yourself."
Dietrich’s frown deepened.
His sister was found?
This was good!
He had always been worried about her because she had that trash good for nothing Custodes that was now even fucking dead, that useless trash.
He had always hated that arrogant and prideful look on that Luxuria.
Now that he was dead, he would simply find someone sufficient enough for his Sister even in this Settlement, someone who would even give her a greater edge to survive.
He looked toward Ealdor Ubergulden Marxist.
The old man met his gaze and nodded with the composed authority of someone accustomed to delegating matters below his threshold of direct concern.
"Go," Marxist said.
"Handle it."
Dietrich stepped out of the compound with the others moving behind him, his Custos taking her position at his right, the alarm still sounding through the wall’s architecture in its rhythmic pulse.

The Silurian who had delivered the news walked ahead without further elaboration, which meant what awaited outside the compound walls was something for which no elaboration would have been adequate preparation.
His sister had found the Settlement.
And something had struck THE Bellum Pulse of THE Scales hard enough to trigger the alarm.
He walked faster as he pieced together how the two were connected!

chapters.title: Chapter 5306: Settlement III
paragraphs: The settlement had taken shape through the application of excess toward the production of impressiveness.

Bone-reinforced structures rose across the compound’s interior in tight clusters, the material coming from Galdr Source Beasts whose skeletons carried residual Source energy that the builders had incorporated deliberately, the walls and housing units and storage facilities all carrying the faint ambient warmth of things built from formerly powerful things.

The Superbius quarters were the tallest. The Ira barracks were the widest. The Acedia administrative structures sat between them with the functional sobriety of builders who had been told to make something useful and had done exactly that and nothing more.
Together they formed a settlement that communicated, without any particular subtlety, the hierarchy of the beings occupying it.
Dietrich moved through it quickly.

He and the others floated upward as they neared the perimeter wall, the alarm still sounding through THE Bellum Pulse of THE Scales in its rhythmic report, and the Gilded Ones throughout the settlement had stopped what they were doing. Dozens of them stood looking upward toward the top of the wall.
He followed their gaze.
Two figures stood at the wall’s crest.
The wall’s surface was actively trying to remove them.

THE Bellum Pulse ran through the entire perimeter construction continuously, the defensive mechanism pressing outward against any Source expression that contacted it, and the figures standing on top of it had their lower bodies vibrating with the pressure of the Pulse working against their presence with the full force of every Gilded One in the settlement whose power had been fed into its reinforcement.
They were standing there anyway!
Dietrich recognized his sister first.

Ubergulden Adelheid! Alive, standing, her Galdr Source burning with a density that made him blink because it was considerably more than even he, the development visible in how her foundations pressed against the surrounding air.
The Custos stood beside her.
The Luxuria. The one who should have been dead, whose absence from the thread outside THE Advent Wall had made things clear!
Yet...

He was not dissolved. He was standing on top of THE Bellum Pulse of THE Scales wall with his legs absorbing the Pulse’s continuous pressure without visible effort, the multicolored Infinity around his frame dense and concentrated and entirely unbothered by what the wall was attempting to do to him.
Dietrich floated up.
His eyes found his sister’s.
Then the Custos turned his head, and their eyes met, and the Custos smiled and lifted one hand and waved.
Then his left hand moved to Eon’s waist and pulled her in.
Eon’s expression shifted into something exasperated rather than protesting!
Something hot moved through Dietrich’s chest.
How dare this Luxuria put his hands on his sister like that?! In front of everyone!
Standing on the settlement wall like he owned the approach. He had warned that fucker. He had made himself clear in the Braneworld!
He had communicated the boundaries of acceptable behavior and this Luxuria had apparently filed that communication somewhere he couldn’t locate it.
Dietrich rose toward them.
"Little Thing." His voice came out cold."I warned you, didn’t I? Come down from there."

He reached for his Galdr Source and extended a pulling force toward the Custos, the authority of his foundations pressing outward in the expression of a senior Gilded One correcting the positioning of a Luxuria who had forgotten the demarcations of his station. It was not an attack. It was a demonstration.
Yet...
The Custos floated where he was.
Nothing happened.

Dietrich’s frown went deep. He pushed harder. The Custos stood on the wall with the concentrated Infinity dense around him and looked back at Dietrich with the calm patience of someone watching a process run its course.
Eon opened her mouth.
"Don’t." Dietrich cut across her without looking at her. "Sister, say nothing. This Luxuria needs to be shown their place."
The Custos looked at him.
His eyes were cold!
"She was trying to save her brother from humiliation," he said. "A worthy effort. But some people can’t be saved."
He paused.
"You only live today because you share blood relations."
BOOM!

Dietrich met the ground before he understood what had redirected him toward it. One moment he was in the air, the next a force had found him, and the force crushed him down and left a crater in the settlement floor!
It left him at its center looking up at the sky with blood in his mouth and a ringing in his foundations that had nothing to do with THE Bellum Pulse.
He lay there!

He was Superbius. He was Ubergulden. He was Silurian Paleozoic Scale with Prime Cause integrations and the full weight of one of the greatest Houses in THE Braneworld behind his name. And a Luxuria Custodes had just put him in a crater in his own settlement!
Around the crater, the settlement had gone very quiet.
Dozens of Seidr and Galdr Source Superbius and Ira Gilded Ones stood in the surrounding space with incredulity!
A Sororis Prima at Galdr Source raised her hands toward the two figures still standing on the wall, her voice careful and powerful as she sensed something heavy between thr impact just then!
"What is this? We are all of THE Ubergulden House here, and clear demarcations exist. Why is the first thing you come with conflict?"

"We naturally came to advance the glory of Gilded Ones." The Custos looked down at her with the expression of someone sharing obvious information. "We came... for whatever intelligence this settlement has collected over the time you’ve been here. So we can use it to advance ahead and spread that glory further."
The silence that followed was the settlement processing what it had just heard.
A Luxuria speaking to a Sororis Prima this way was not a thing that happened. A Luxuria speaking to a Superbius this way was not a thing that happened!

A Luxuria standing on THE Bellum Pulse of THE Scales absorbing its continuous pressure without visible effort, having just put a Silurian Paleozoic Ubergulden in a crater, and then addressing the senior members of the settlement like he was conducting a briefing, was not a thing that had a framework for happening!
Nobody moved.
Nobody was willing to be the next one to test what happened!
