chapters.title: Chapter 5307: Settlement IV
paragraphs: Pride was a fascinating thing to observe in beings who hadn’t earned it.

There was a version of pride that existed because it had been produced naturally, forged through genuine adversity and genuine achievement and the earned confidence of someone who had looked at something difficult and come out the other side of it changed.
That version had weight. It pushed back!
It made decisions regardless of consequence because it had calculated the consequence and found the consequence acceptable.

Then there was engineered pride. Superbius pride. The kind cultivated into a being’s foundations through careful Gilded methodology, installed the way any other capability was installed, present as a feature of the existence rather than as a truth of the being. It looked identical from a distance. Up close, it revealed itself the moment a real test arrived.
The test had arrived.

Noah had smashed Dietrich into the ground in front of dozens of Superbius and Ira Gilded Ones and all of them had stood exactly where they were, assessing. Which was sensible. He wasn’t criticizing the intelligence of the calculation.
But intelligence and pride were different faculties, and every one of them standing still while one of their own bled in a crater was giving him information about which faculty was running the room.

None of the big ones had shown up yet. The heavy power sat deeper in the settlement, further from the wall. What he had in front of him were Seidr Source and Galdr Source Gilded Ones, which was still Paleozoic Scale, still formidable by any standard he had operated within before THE Source Lands.
They were watching him stand on THE Bellum Pulse wall and absorb its continuous pressure and they were making correct assessments about the gap between what they were and what he appeared to be.
He actually wanted to be problematic!

He wanted a fight. He genuinely wanted one. He had come into this settlement carrying the accumulated weight of the Arms Race and the Persevere spamming and a Galdr Source so saturated it had pressed against its own ceiling, and he had been hoping at least one of them would give him a reason to test it.
Not one of them moved.
He looked down at them.
"You know, I always looked up to Superbius."He said it pleasantly, with the tone of someone sharing a sincere memory.

"Oh, Superbius! As a lowly Luxuria, my status was just pleasure and nothing else. I knew the stories though. Superbius and Ira fighting against Source Lifeforms and Infinite Lifeforms, standing at the front of every major conflict in our Gilded history, moving forward when everything said stop."He looked across the gathered Gilded Ones slowly.

"I thought, wow. If only I could do something like that. So I worked hard and I became the Custos of a Superbius Gilded One. I entered THE Source Lands. And now I stand in front of more Superbius Gilded Ones than I have ever seen in one place."
He paused.

"Where... is your pride?" He asked it genuinely, without aggression. "Does a Luxuria like me ever have the chance to move past my designated engineering? Will your pride allow that? Or will you stand there watching one of your own lie in a crater and decidetoday is not the day?"
BOOM!
He let the aura drop.

The Infinite Radiation of his Source came down across the settlement in a wave that carried the full pressure of what he had become across the last several hours, the dense concentrated multicolored flames around his frame expanding outward as the heat of it crashed into the surrounding Superbius and Ira Gilded Ones and pressed against their foundations from above!
BOOM!
He looked down at them.
These were the fucking people who had authorized the Existential Acedia Ordnances. Or connected to the people who had.

The House that had looked at the lower Observable Existence with its countless Quintillions of beings and its Early Creatures and its Living Existences and its Fold Dwellers and had signed off on the calculation that made all of that an acceptable cost.
These dumb motherfuckers, standing in their bone-reinforced settlement with their engineered pride and their Galdr Source capabilities and their careful assessments.
"WHERE IS YOUR PRIDE?!"

The bellow came out carrying the Prime Cause of Tyranny behind it, the foundational truth of hierarchy pressed outward in a wave that didn’t ask whether the beings it was reaching had opinions about kneeling.
The Tyranny didn’t argue with resistance. It simply told existence what the order was!
The wave moved through the settlement as it was going to make them kneel!
A golden glow intercepted it at that moment!

The glow came from the direction of the settlement’s interior, warm and dense and carrying the weight of a Source that had been developing in THE Source Lands for considerably longer than anyone else present. It buzzed against the Tyranny wave and held it at the settlement’s edge, not dispersing it but matching it, the two pressures finding each other and establishing a standoff.
An old man walked through the gap.
Marxist moved with the unhurried confidence of something that had not been concerned about this situation from the moment it heard the alarm and had taken the time to assess properly before arriving.
His Source garments of beast skin and bone pressed outward with their own ambient pressure. His eyes, sharp beneath the bald head and the long golden beard, were bright with genuine interest.
He looked at Noah.
Then he laughed.
"An exceptional Luxuria among our Gilded lineage!" He said it with the warmth of someone who had found something they had been looking for without knowing they were looking.

"You are right to feel stifled. Someone with what you carry lying back in the throes of pleasure would have been a waste of considerable potential." He raised a hand toward the settlement around him. "We will welcome you here with every grievance intact. Pride is power. This is not a saying. It is the foundational truth of what we are."
He walked forward slowly.

"Look at the beings standing around us who did not step forward when you challenged them. They are not cowards. They are simply beings with less power than you demonstrated, and beings with less power naturally carry less pride, because pride without the foundation to back it collapses under real pressure." He stopped a comfortable distance from the wall.

"You, a Luxuria by designation, carried more pride into this settlement today than every Superbius here because your power exceeded what your designation suggested. That is the only measure that matters in existence."His eyes held Noah’s.
"We need every fragment of power and pride we can find in these lands. You are clearly carrying more than your designation assigned you. That makes you precisely what we need."
He spread his hands.
"Welcome."
Noah looked at him with cold eyes.
The old man was shrewd!

chapters.title: Chapter 5308: Barbarian! I
paragraphs: The old man finished speaking and Ruination’s prompts arrived before the silence after the words had fully settled.
|Ealdor Ubergulden Marxist- behavioral analysis.|

|Under standard Gilded social architecture, what you just did would have produced a very different response. A Luxuria humiliating a Superbius Gilded One in public, releasing Source pressure against an assembled group, none of that gets welcomed. None of that gets a philosophical monologue about pride being power. That gets corrected, hard, by whoever is senior enough to do the correcting.|

|Marxist is that senior. He is choosing not to correct you. The only reason a being of his standing makes that choice is that he assessed your power and decided it was worth more to him than the social cost of letting a Luxuria stand where you are standing.|
|He wants to use you for something. The welcome is real in the sense that he genuinely wants your cooperation. The goodwill behind it is not.|

Noah read through the analysis while keeping his face arranged around pleasant attention. Nothing Ruination had surfaced was surprising. He had already read Marxist the moment the old man walked through the settlement and laughed instead of escalating.
Marxist smiled.
"The prideful lead among us regardless of designation. You have demonstrated more than enough to stand in the company of Superbius leaders." He looked at Noah with warmth.
"What is your name?"
Noah smiled back.
"I gave myself a new name as I break the common mold of Luxuria." He held Marxist’s eyes. "I am THE Infinite Speaker, Ozymandias."
BOOM!
The name landed in the settlement.
Ozymandias! He had used the designation of one of the bodies contained within his own existence!

Marxist’s smile deepened. He reached down and lifted Dietrich from the crater with the authority of a man tidying up before company, dusting him off with two businesslike strokes of his hand that communicated, without any ambiguity, that Dietrich was furniture for the purposes of this conversation.
"Ozymandias." He tested the name.
"You came seeking opportunity. I will give you one." He gestured somewhere behind him, further into the interior.

"At a distance from here we were planning a push through a concentrated group of Source Beasts. The weakest among them are Galdr Source. They surround a resource of immense power connected to THE Primordial Source."
His eyes held Noah’s.
"As someone so supremely filled with pride and power, why don’t you act as one of our swords? Pierce through the Source Beast armies for us."
Noah smiled brilliantly.
He had come looking for opportunities. He had found one, and the opportunity had found him at the same time, and both of them were now looking at each other and running calculations.
Marxist’s calculation: exceptional power, unknown origin, can be used as a battering ram against Source Beast armies and then disposed of or absorbed into the structure depending on what survived.

His calculation: a resource connected to THE Primordial Source, information about its location and what surrounded it, a Gilded settlement’s worth of collected intelligence, and a mission that conveniently pointed him exactly where he wanted to go.

He jumped down from the wall, keeping Eon close, and landed in front of Marxist and the circle of powerful Gilded Ones around him, all of them with Sources exceeding Galdr, all of them watching him coldly as their power was genuine!
His own...was just approaching there ridiculously because of spamming Persevere every second for thousands upon thousands of seconds!
He looked at them and smiled at all of them.
"Hey, for the glory of Gilded Ones, right?"He kept his voice pleasant. "It’s not like you’re planning on sending me to my death in those Source Beast armies. Haha!"
Marxist laughed.
"Bahaha! Right! Come, let us feast on some truly delicate Source Beast meat and we will set off soon after!"
The two of them looked at each other.

Both sides could read exactly what the other was thinking. It was visible in the eyes and the smiles that two beings produced when they had decided to cooperate while fully understanding that cooperation was a temporary state with an expiration date neither of them was going to acknowledge out loud.
It fit what both of them wanted. So they went along with it!
Noah moved deeper into the settlement, passing Dietrich on the way. Dietrich was containing himself with the visible effort, every muscle in his frame communicating fury.
Noah smiled and waved as he moved on.
Eon’s voice came into his mind as they walked.

"They...are still my people. I want to change them and how they do things. But it would be meaningful if the path wasn’t entirely built on slaughter. I know blood will be spilled. Let us just do our best that endless seas of Gilded blood don’t fall."
She was pleading for her brother. For her House. For the people she had been born into and had spent her existence among, regardless of what those people had chosen to become.
Noah mulled over her words as the settlement’s structures passed around them.
He nodded lightly.

Blood would be spilled. Rivers of it, probably. That was already decided by the decisions that had already been made by people who were not him. But rivers were not the same as endless seas, and he had some influence over the difference!
But while he made progress in THE Source Lands, he also sensed thr budding moment of progression for a certain Evolutionary Arms Race as he and THE Infiniverse were at the precipice of change!
Finally, the thousands upon thousands of spammed Exelissomai were about to show their effect!
In THE Infiniverse.
WUU! WUU!

Fireballs came from everywhere he was at once, plasmic clusters of condensed Osmontian Absolute Infinity released in every direction simultaneously, Quintillions of them spreading outward across THE Early Veiled Shore in a continuous omnidirectional release that turned the air around him into a field neither THE Creature nor Calypso could close distance through without eating whatever they ran into.
THE Creature had tried twice. Calypso had tried once. Both had pulled back.
Noah kept generating as his entire existence was running on an endless thrill of infinity!
Then the sea above moved and exploded!

chapters.title: Chapter 5309: Barbarian! II
paragraphs: The sea had been churning throughout the Arms Race, the Environmental Pressure cycling through its phases as THE Infiniverse managed each one, but what it did now was different from anything it had done across the preceding nine hours.

The sea expanded, doubling in density, then doubling again, then again, the obsidian concentration above THE Early Veiled Shore growing dozens of times larger than it had been at any prior point until the sky above the shore had become a solid mass of compressed Primordial Source energy pressing against the upper layers of the domain.
The sea turned into incandescent obsidian flames!
Then it fell!
BOOM!

The obsidian flames rushed downward across THE Early Veiled Shore and beyond it, spreading across THE Infiniverse’s full expanse in a wave that reached THE Creature’s position and Calypso’s position and Noah’s position simultaneously, the Arms Race delivering its final distribution to all three participants at once.
Noah took sixty percent of it.

The flames went where they went, drawn by whatever calculus the Prime Exelissomai had been running across the full nine hours of the Arms Race, and sixty percent of what the sea above had produced found Noah’s foundations and pressed into them with the weight of something that had been accumulating specifically for this moment.
BOOM!
|Evolutionary Arms Race: Concluded.|

|The Prime Exelissomai process has registered sufficient pressure accumulation and resonance to signal completion. Total utterances of Exelissomai across the Arms Race duration:approximately 32,400.All utterances have been compounded into the first utterance’s ongoing process as confirmed at the Arms Race’s initiation.|
|Result:Pure Primordial Essenceis being introduced into your existence at the volume and purity corresponding to the compounded stack.|

|Pure Primordial Essence: The undifferentiated energy that precedes all differentiated things. Before THE First Cause established the first distinction between what existence would be and what it would not be, before any Prime Cause or Observable Existence or Civilization or being had been produced, there was Pure Primordial Essence.|

|It is the energy of the state that existed before existence decided what it was going to become. It carries no alignment, no Cause expression, no identity, only the raw authority of potential before potential resolved into anything. Source Lifeforms, at the moment of their emergence, are cultivated with small volumes of this energy. It is what makes them what they are rather than what anything else is.|

|Due to the compounded stack of 32,400 Prime Exelissomai utterances, the volume and purity ofPure Primordial Essencebeing introduced to your existence exceeds what an emerging Source Lifeform receives by more than one million times. Your Infinity, your blood, your Causes, your Galdr Source, your Observable and Unobservable Force, THE Infiniverse- all are receiving this simultaneously.|
HUUM!
Noah felt it arrive.

The Pure Primordial Essence moved through him. It wasn’t attacking a target or reinforcing a structure or elevating a specific component. It was filling the spaces between everything he was, the gaps between his Infinity and his Causes and his Osmontian Absolute Infinity and his Galdr Source, settling into the foundational layer beneath all of these as though it had always been meant to occupy that layer and had simply been waiting for a volume large enough to actually do it.
His blood burned with it.

His Causes received it and responded by expressing themselves at amplitudes they had not expressed at before, the nine Prime Causes burning through their respective regions of THE Infiniverse with the additional depth that Pure Primordial Essence added when it moved through a Cause connection.
THE Infiniverse herself received her share and her nine Prime Cause regions blazed accordingly.

|Secondary result:The letter of Persevere has accumulated sufficient Pure Primordial Essence through the compounded stack to trigger elevation. Persevere is now the Prime Letter of Persevere.Its effects, cost routing, and compounding capacity have been elevated by the same margin as the Prime Letter of Exelissomai relative to its standard version. Infinity pays the cost. The elevation is permanent.|
|Tertiary result: An anomaly has been identified in the distribution of Pure Primordial Essence as it interacts with your foundational architecture.|

|You do not exist on Vakochev’s Scales of Existence. This is established. The Pure Primordial Essence entering your foundations has nowhere to funnel your evolution because no established path in any known framework accounts for what you are.|

|As a result, the evolutionary process has produced something outside all established categories. You arewild, unlearned, and unknownwithin the framework of THE Primordial Source’s understanding of what beings can be. The Pure Primordial Essence has therefore not refined you toward any existing path. It has recognized you as a new category and produced the corresponding factor.|
|THE Infinite Anomalous Source Factor of THE Source Barbarian has emerged.|

|THE Source Barbarianis not a designation. It is a recognition- that you exist outside all Scales, outside all established Source Lifeform emergence paths, outside the architecture that THE Primordial Source uses to categorize the beings within existence. The Factor does not constrain this. It amplifies it.Your evolution does not follow any road because no road leads where you are going.|

|One of the preliminary things thatTHE Source Barbarian Factorgrants the capacity to absorb and convert Source energies from any category without requiring compatibility, since compatibility requires being categorized and you are not categorized. It is wild because you are wild. It is infinite because you are.|
BOOM!

The obsidian flames of the Pure Primordial Essence settled around Noah’s figure in dense slow-churning waves that had nothing in common with the Persevere flames or the nine Prime Cause expressions or the multicolored Osmontian Absolute Infinity.
They were something else, older than all of those things, carrying the weight of a state that had existed before categories had been assigned to anything.
He burned with it.
He burned and seamlessly absorbed Pure Primordial Essence as his cells drank hungrily and richly!
And he felt all his weavings of Existence being sublimated and...well, not truly changing as much as elevate Quintessentially.
It was really Evolution, basic and simple!

chapters.title: Chapter 5310: Barbarian! III
paragraphs: In the far reaches of THE Early Veiled Shore, two figures were also burning.

THE Creature stood in his own elevation, the Pure Primordial Essence that had reached him moving through his ancient rebuilt foundations and adding to what was already there, the obsidian flames of his own Primordial Source expression burning brighter as the Arms Race delivered its result to him!

Calypso received hers, the Relictus’s vast ancient frame processing the Pure Primordial Essence with the depth of something that had cultivated with this energy across eons and knew what it was receiving.
Both of them looked toward Noah.

The obsidian flames around him were not the same flames burning around them. The density was wrong. The volume was wrong. The way the air around him trembled and sparked and seemed to treat the space immediately adjacent to his position as a different category of space was wrong.

THE Creature had a Source that had been refined by adversity across longer than most frameworks extended. Calypso had a Source that had been present since before most of existence could remember its own earliest events.
What was emerging around Noah felt like something that hadn’t happened before.

They watched it, somber and still, the two most ancient beings in the Arms Race looking at the youngest and feeling the distance between what they were receiving and what he was receiving as a physical condition of the space between them.
Something grand was coming out of that obsidian fire.
Neither of them was certain what it would look like when it arrived!
The first thing Noah felt was the scales.

Not new scales. The Primus Apeiron form had always carried its multicolored obsidian scales across every surface of his frame, but what settled over him now was different from those. Thinner. More complete. A layer that wasn’t armor but expression, the Primus Apeiron capabilities becoming permanent rather than accessed through different bodies, pressing outward through the Pure Primordial Essence and fusing into something that covered his entire existence as a continuous living surface.
Obsidian gold.

The color of it was the result of everything being integrated simultaneously, the Primus Apeiron and the Pillar of Infinity and every Actualized Civilization within it and the Observable Force and the Unobservable Force and the Osmontian Absolute Infinity and the Galdr Source and the full backing of THE Infinite Cause and the nine Prime Causes all finding positions within the same layer, the layer organizing them not as separate systems but as one continuous expression.
|THE Aura of THE Source Barbarian: Formed.|
|The Pure Primordial Essence produced by the Prime Exelissomai utterances has integrated all active capabilities into a single unified outer expression. Contents of THE Aura of THE Source Barbarian:|
|Primus Apeiron Form capabilities: Permanently expressed. No activation required. The form’s full physical and foundational capabilities are active at all times through the Aura layer.|

|Actualized Civilizations from THE Hadean Pillar of Infinity: Fully integrated into the Aura. THE Cheating Architect, THE Protagonist, Perpetual Harvest, and all other Actualized Civilizations now function as permanent ambient conditions of your existence rather than capabilities you access.|
|Observable Force and Unobservable Force: Woven into the Aura layer’s surface, producing continuous dual expression across your full existence simultaneously.|

|Osmontian Absolute Infinity: Runs as the Aura’s foundational medium. Everything integrated into the Aura expresses itself through Osmontian Absolute Infinity, meaning every capability within the Aura carries your identity as its carrier.|
|Galdr Source: Integrated as the Aura’s Source foundation, the density of it compounded by nine hours of Arms Race development and 32,400 Exelissomai utterances.|
|THE Infinite Cause and all integrated Prime Causes: Active as governing truths of the Aura’s expression, their Prime Cause lights now visible across the Aura’s surface continuously.|

|Operational character: THE Source Barbarian Aura does not select capabilities for deployment. It expresses all of them simultaneously at all times, the wild and anomalistic nature of THE Source Barbarian Factor amplifying every component through brute force, both close range and long range. You do not aim a specific tool at a specific problem. You bring the full weight of everything you are to every point of contact. This is what it means to be wild in existence.|
BOOM!
The obsidian gold rose from him.

Not as light. As mass, the Aura pressing outward from every surface of his frame and expanding with the weight of everything it contained, the nearby air shuddering at the contact as existence registered something it didn’t have a category for. The early veiled shore’s golden sands trembled beneath him.
HUUM!
He began to grow!
Grow! Grow! Grow!

The process was unhurried. His frame expanded in every dimension without violence, the Pure Primordial Essence and the Aura of THE Source Barbarian pushing his physical expression outward toward the size that the Barbarian Factor recognized as his preliminary body.

His musculature expanded with his scale, every proportion maintained, the definition of his frame becoming something that light behaved differently around as it grew to a size where light had time to notice it.
He stopped at one Gigaparsec.
He floated in THE Early Veiled Shore at a scale where the shore’s golden sands were a surface beneath him that he could sit on comfortably!

The obsidian gold of the Aura covered everything, the nine Prime Cause lights running across it in their continuous expression, the Observable and Unobservable Force currents moving through the surface in their parallel rivers, the Osmontian Absolute Infinity blazing through the full scale of it!
He raised his hands.
They were enormous. He looked at them with the calm attention of someone taking inventory.

He pressed his palm slightly. A test. The Aura of THE Source Barbarian responded with the simultaneous activation of everything within it directed toward that pressure, and he felt with complete clarity what applying that pressure to a Devonian Paleozoic Scale being would produce.
Shattering.
He looked at the space where his Galdr Source expression pressed outward through the Aura and thought what that expression could do to a common Galdr Source Lifeform if he closed his fist around one.
Crushed in an instant!

He looked at the full expression of what he was at this scale with the Aura covering every coordinate of his existence and the nine Prime Cause lights blazing and the Osmontian Absolute Infinity running through everything.
Fourth Scale entities felt manageable.

He couldn’t say it with certainty. He would need to actually test it to say it with certainty, and he was aware that the gap between feeling something and confirming something. But the feeling was there!
Calypso was a Relictus. She had been a Relictus since before most of existence could date its own earliest memories.
He thought he could wound her now.
Him! Still operating within his First Infinite Scale! Still at the beginning of what THE Infinite Scale of Existence was designed to contain!
He looked at his massive obsidian gold hands again in the golden light of THE Early Veiled Shore.

Then he looked at where THE Creature and Calypso floated in the distance, their own elevations burning around them, both of them watching the gigaparsec figure that had emerged from the obsidian fire with the somber attention of Source Lifeforms.
Because at this moment, while Noah had not grasped THE Primordial Source, his body gave off a pure aura...similar to a Relictus as he was filled with boundless seas of Pure Primordial Essence!

As mass, the Aura pressing outward from every surface of his frame and expanding with the weight of everything it contained, the nearby air shuddering at the contact as existence registered something it didn’t have a category for.
The early veiled shore’s golden sands trembled beneath him.
HUUM!
He began to grow!
Grow!
Grow!
Grow!
The process was unhurried.

His frame expanded in every dimension without violence, the Pure Primordial Essence and the Aura of THE Source Barbarian pushing his physical expression outward toward the size that the Barbarian Factor recognized as his preliminary body.

His musculature expanded with his scale, every proportion maintained, the definition of his frame becoming something that light behaved differently around as it grew to a size where light had time to notice it.
He stopped at one Gigaparsec.
He floated in THE Early Veiled Shore at a scale where the shore’s golden sands were a surface beneath him that he could sit on comfortably!

The obsidian gold of the Aura covered everything, the nine Prime Cause lights running across it in their continuous expression, the Observable and Unobservable Force currents moving through the surface in their parallel rivers, the Osmontian Absolute Infinity blazing through the full scale of it!
He raised his hands.
They were enormous.
He looked at them with the calm attention of someone taking inventory.
He pressed his palm slightly.
A test.

The Aura of THE Source Barbarian responded with the simultaneous activation of everything within it directed toward that pressure, and he felt with complete clarity what applying that pressure to a Devonian Paleozoic Scale being would produce.
Shattering.
He looked at the space where his Galdr Source expression pressed outward through the Aura and thought what that expression could do to a common Galdr Source Lifeform if he closed his fist around one.
Crushed in an instant!

He looked at the full expression of what he was at this scale with the Aura covering every coordinate of his existence and the nine Prime Cause lights blazing and the Osmontian Absolute Infinity running through everything.
Fourth Scale entities felt manageable.
He couldn’t say it with certainty.
He would need to actually test it to say it with certainty, and he was aware that the gap between feeling something and confirming something.
But the feeling was there!
Calypso was a Relictus.
She had been a Relictus since before most of existence could date its own earliest memories.
He thought he could wound her now.
Him!
Still operating within his First Infinite Scale!
Still at the beginning of what THE Infinite Scale of Existence was designed to contain!
He looked at his massive obsidian gold hands again in the golden light of THE Early Veiled Shore.

Then he looked at where THE Creature and Calypso floated in the distance, their own elevations burning around them, both of them watching the gigaparsec figure that had emerged from the obsidian fire with the somber attention of Source Lifeforms.
Because at this moment, while Noah had not grasped THE Primordial Source, his body gave off a pure aura...similar to a Relictus as he was filled with boundless seas of Pure Primordial Essence!

chapters.title: Chapter 5311: Sword I
paragraphs: He looked gloriously titanic, and he let himself enjoy it!

He had spent his existence climbing from nothing toward something, and this was a moment where the something had become considerably more than it had been a day ago, and a being who couldn’t enjoy that was a being who had forgotten why they were climbing in the first place.
One must never forget!

He floated at his reduced scale now, no longer a gigaparsec titan but carrying the weight of one regardless, the obsidian gold of THE Aura of THE Source Barbarian running across his body in continuous expression.
His path remained good. He could finalize his First Infinite Scale soon. When he did, he could choose a name for it. Or he could choose not to. He would see how he felt when he arrived.

|Arms Race conclusion protocol: The Source Lifeforms called forth by Prime Exelissomai as Biotic Pressure will now be dismissed. Their participation in the Evolutionary Arms Race is complete. They have received their share of the result and will be returned to their prior positions.|
Noah looked at THE Creature and Calypso.

Obsidian light was already beginning to wrap around both of them, the Prime Exelissomai recalling its Biotic Pressures now that the process had concluded. And as the light moved over them, his perception found what sat inside both of those ancient bodies.
THE Primordial Source.

It ran through THE Creature and through Calypso at the foundational level, the direct unmediated presence that made them what they were, and Noah’s eyes flashed with something he didn’t bother to suppress.
Hunger.

He would have THE Primordial Source in his hands eventually! He had Pure Primordial Essence right now, flooding through him at over a million times an emerging Source Lifeform’s volume, melding into his Infinity in a process that felt grander with every second it continued. That was the precursor.
The actual Source was the destination, and looking at it inside two beings who carried it natively only sharpened the appetite he had developed for reaching it.
But that was later.
He took a step and appeared before the two of them.
"We all benefited," he said. "But thank you for the challenge."

Calypso nodded, the ancient Relictus acknowledging the words with the economy of a being who had answered the call of a Prime Letter, received what it came for, and saw no reason to add anything to the transaction.
THE Creature looked at him.
"Don’t underestimate THE Gilded Ones."His voice carried the somber weight it always carried.

"In existence there are Infinite Lifeforms and Source Lifeforms. There are Bounded Lifeforms, Gilded Lifeforms, Primeval Lifeforms. THE Gilded Ones were not always in the position they hold now, and yet they have climbed to a place where they fight against Infinite Lifeforms and Source Lifeforms directly."
He held Noah’s eyes.
"Existence is vast and filled with boundless terrors. Be careful."
HUUM!
The obsidian brilliance closed over him, and THE Creature was gone.
Noah stood with the words for a moment.
He took them seriously. THE Creature did not waste warnings, and a being who had existed across the eons THE Creature had existed across did not describe something as a boundless terror casually.

THE Gilded Ones had nuked an entire Observable Existence as a routine administrative solution. He had already seen what they were willing to do. THE Creature was telling him he had not yet seen the full scale of what they were capable of, and that was worth knowing!
He breathed in and turned toward the vastness of THE Infiniverse.
He had not been the only one to change.
THE Infiniverse had been bathed in Pure Primordial Essence alongside him, her share flooding into her substrate and her nine Prime Cause regions and her seas of Observable and Unobservable Force.

And the change moving through her was more gradual than his because she was countless gigaparsecs vast and a change at that scale took time to complete. She radiated an ancient air now, the quality of a domain that had existed for far longer than it actually had, the Pure Primordial Essence aging her presence into something that felt foundational.

She was frightening. Apart from him, THE Infiniverse was genuinely frightening in power, an autonomous cognizant Observable Existence carrying nine Prime Causes and seas of dual Force and now Pure Primordial Essence woven through all of it.
And then there was his mother.

Amelia Osmont. The Origin of THE Infinite Cause. Her power had been rising tremendously since the emergence, the Cause that had originated from her turning back to elevate its source. If she ever decided to throw her hands against anyone...
Oh boy!
He filed that thought with a faint internal amusement and finally remembered the woman he had brought here.

His body reduced in size as he descended to the golden sands of THE Early Veiled Shore, coming down near where Taylor sat next to the grave she had dug for herself hours ago when the Environmental Pressure first began.
She had not, in the end, needed it.
She looked up at him and shook her head slowly.
"You are a ridiculous existence," she said.
Noah looked at her.
"The promise of safety for you and Adrastia was fulfilled," he said. "But you haven’t been returned to your Observable Existence yet..."
Taylor waved a hand dismissively before he finished.

"Promises altered from the other side are our weight to bear, not yours."She brushed sand off her legs. "Achilles Adrastia already has a main body back in his home Observable Existence. And mine, well. Both of us got taken to a home base of Source Lifeforms by Sir William. The Cornwall Observable Existence. I’m guessing it’s a base of THE Swords of Existence, and we’re there to undergo trials to become Attendants of Existence."She shrugged.

"I made that choice myself. So that promise is null and void. This sliver of my existence here, I can disperse it, or I can call forth my other self to take it over and expand this vessel into a main body. She can connect to the people of my Observable Existence easily enough."A pause, and something sharpened behind her rapid eyes.
"She’s a troublemaker, so I usually keep her down. But these Gilded Ones freely nuked an entire Observable Existence. I want to make trouble for them! I’m still defiant on that."

chapters.title: Chapter 5312: Sword II
paragraphs: Noah smiled.
He thought about the suit and the blade Sir William had given him, and about the many paths laid out in front of him, all of them active, all of them running at once.

His body as Dante in THE Sanctum Velanthra would be grasping the Third Cause within those depths. His body in THE Source Lands would be leaving with the Gilded Ones of Marxist’s settlement to seek an unknown Source treasure surrounded by Source Beast armies.

Gathering information on the reach of Gilded Ones into THE Source Lands was also ongoing as he felt like with settlements, so long as they were desperate enough, more and more would arrive on THE Strand of Broken Scales.

They didn’t send powerful Gilded Ones over en masse as they didn’t wish to risk their lives with too many unknowns, but when they sent more and more beings like Marxist...they would be able to make a lot of headway!
But apart from this...
There was the pathway of THE Sword of Existence in front of him now, waiting. And he still had to finish defining his First Infinite Scale.
There was much to be done.
That was fine. Being busy meant progressing, and progressing meant moving forward, and moving forward was the only direction he had ever genuinely respected!
He could not remain static!
So he would push ahead on all of it!

His biggest aim, the one that sat behind all the others, was grasping THE Primordial Source. A task that countless beings across existence had found impossibly hard, that ancient Source Lifeforms guarded as the thing that made them what they were, that THE Gilded Ones were building entire settlements in THE Source Lands to inch toward.
THE Source Lands was one possibility.
THE Sword of Existence was another.
So.

He reached into his existence and took out the suit and the blade Sir William Arthur had given him. The Lesser Existential Source Armament sat there in obsidian and white, the blue-obsidian sheath of THE Sovereign Reckoning resting beside it, both of them carrying the quiet weight of instruments forged by a Source Lifeform for a specific purpose.
He looked at the suit.
He was ready to put it on and see exactly what barrier he had to cross to become...a Sword of Existence.
<Swords of Existence>

Of the Swords of Existence, little is recorded that can be trusted, and much is recorded that cannot, for they are not a people who keep records of themselves and they discourage the keeping of records by others.
What follows is assembled from the fragments that survived, and one is asked to hold it loosely.

They are Lifeforms, though the word strains under the weight of what it is asked to carry when applied to them. Some were born of Infinity. Some emerged from THE Primordial Source itself. Some began as lesser things and climbed, across eons of adversity, to the threshold where the Swords would consider them at all.

What unites them is not their origin, for their origins could not be more varied, but the standard they have chosen to answer to, which is THE Primordial Source, and the Way each of them carries within, which is theirs alone and answers to nothing beneath the Source.
They are not protectors, though they protect. They are not destroyers, though they destroy!

To call them either is to mistake the consequence of their actions for the cause of them, and this mistake has been made by nearly everyone who has ever encountered them and lived to record the encounter.
Consider theGold Incursion of Infinity.

In an age not too long ago, THE Gilded Ones and a coalition of Infinite Lifeforms fell into a war whose origins are no longer clear and whose conduct is remembered with horror by every chronicle that mentions it at all.

Multiple Observable Existences became the battleground. Both were laid to waste in the fighting, their populations caught between forces that did not pause to consider them, their substrates torn apart by weapons that neither side had any intention of restraining.
Countless died who had no part in the quarrel. The Observable Existences, which had existed for longer than most things existed, were reduced to ruin in the span of a single drawn-out atrocity.
The Swords of Existence stepped in.

They did not appeal to the better natures of the combatants, having correctly assessed that no such natures were present. They entered the war and inflicted casualties on both sides so severe, so indifferent to which banner the dying had marched under, that the war simply could not continue.
THE Gilded Ones lost figures they could not afford to lose. The Infinite Lifeforms lost the same. And in the silence that followed, neither side had the strength remaining to resume!
It is tempting to say the Swords fought for the dying. For the countless caught between the armies. For the ruined Observable Existences and the lives that had been spent in them.
This is not what happened.
The Swords of Existence did not fight for the little ones. They did not weigh the suffering of the innocent and find it moved them to action.

They fought because the war offended THE Source, because the unraveling of two Observable Existences for no purpose THE Source recognized as legitimate was a thing that could not be permitted to continue, and they followed THE Source where it led them.
That the dying were saved was a consequence. It was not the reason!
This is the thing that must be understood about the Swords of Existence, the thing that makes them feared by the powerful in a way that no merely benevolent force could ever be feared.
A benevolent force can be predicted. It will protect what is good and oppose what is cruel, and the wicked can plan around it.
The Swords cannot be planned around, because they do not serve good and they do not oppose cruelty. They serve THE Source, and THE Source serves nothing.
When a Sword arrives, the question is never whether you are innocent or guilty.
The question is only whether you stand where THE Source has decided the cut will fall.

chapters.title: Chapter 5313: Sword III
paragraphs: He put on the suit.

The Lesser Existential Source Armament settled over him with the precision of something made to exact specification, the obsidian jacket finding his body, the white shirt beneath it, the obsidian tie sitting clean against the shirt.
He adjusted it without rushing, and the Source weaving in the composite recognized him the moment the last piece settled.
Taylor was still sitting on the grave she had dug.
"Wowee..." She shook her head slowly. "You really had to do a whole power move of changing right in front of me like that?"

She said it like a complaint. Her eyes said something else entirely, shining with the appreciation of someone who had seen a great many things across a long existence and was filing this one under things worth having seen!
Noah ignored her and reached for the blade.
THE Sovereign Reckoning came to his hand, the blue-obsidian sheath cool against his palm, and with the suit on and the blade in hand, the picture completed itself.
He looked grand! Magisterial!

Obsidian tendrils of light began to swirl around the suit, rising from the Source weaving in slow deliberate spirals, and over all of it THE Aura of THE Source Barbarian glowed across his entire body, the obsidian gold of it running beneath and around the obsidian suit so that the two layers of obsidian, the worn and the innate, complemented rather than competed.
He floated above the golden sands.
"Persevere. Exelissomai."
BOOM!

The multicolored flames and the obsidian gold surged around him simultaneously, the two Prime Letters expressing at once, and the flames spilled outward across THE Early Veiled Shore and beyond it into the vastness of THE Infiniverse, the domain receiving the effects the way she received everything he produced now.

He kept uttering them, every second, the way he had been uttering Persevere, the two Prime Letters refining and elevating his existence with each repetition, THE Aura of THE Source Barbarian growing fractionally more terrifying with every utterance because that was simply what it did now!
Below, Taylor clapped her hands together and whistled, low and appreciative.
The obsidian tendrils that had been forming around the suit since he put it on activated.

He watched them closely as they wove together into a bubble of obsidian light, the Source weaving carrying out exactly what Sir William had described it would do, and the body inside the bubble disappeared.
WAP!

Another of his bodies descended to THE Early Veiled Shore a moment later. He had several to spare. The distribution of his existence across domains meant that sending one off to a trial did not leave him absent from anywhere that mattered.
But the one inside the bubble began crossing the vastness of existence, pulled forward by the mechanism of the Source Armament.
Noah felt his existence being drawn across THE Undefined Gaps of existence,and once more, he left his Observable Existence entirely.

He knew what the Gaps were. He had sent THE Infiniverse into them. He described them as the unclassified regions between defined existence, the spaces of no definition where ordinary beings dissolved.

Experiencing them himself was a different thing from understanding them, and what he experienced was his existence being carried on unstable rivers of undefined potential, the terminal infinity within them pressing against his perception with a density that he could sense would have reduced Second Scale entities to paste through proximity alone.
The Source Armament handled it.

It had a set of directions encoded into its weaving, a destination it was pulling him toward, and it provided sufficient power and protection that he didn’t have to do anything but experience the journey.

He sensed the distant Undefined Weavings of existence moving around him, the raw uncategorized potential of the spaces between defined domains, the terminal infinity running through the obsidian rivers that carried him.
It was, he thought, a genuinely pleasant way to travel.

Surfing on obsidian rivers of terminal infinity in a well-cut suit with a Source Lifeform’s blade in hand, the most dangerous spaces in existence held at a comfortable distance by the armament’s protection.
After what felt like a few minutes, definition began to return.

He sensed it before he arrived in it, the definition of endings and catastrophe and apocalypses, obsidian gray light gathering around him as the Undefined Gaps released him into a defined domain. And the moment the definition settled, his existence recognized what it was recognizing, because he carried many Civilizations related to endings and Apocalypse sat at the forefront of them.
He arrived in a place that was dying.
This Observable Existence stretched around him in the state of something that had been mortally wounded and had not yet finished the slow process of expiring.

Weavings of decaying folds drifted through the space, half-dissolved, the structures that should have held them together failing in slow motion. Torn and destroyed Wheels of Existence hung in the distance, their architecture shattered, the cyclical mechanisms that governed the domain’s continuation broken past any repair he could see.
He felt like he was standing inside the shattered remnants of a Primordial Realm, the scale of the destruction vast enough that individual catastrophes blurred into a single condition.
Split golden mountains burned in the distance with roaring flames of terminal infinity, the fire consuming what it touched and producing nothing, the flame of endings rather than transformation.

Entire portions of the dimensional space carried tears that looked like glass-like cuts across existence itself, the fabric of the domain sliced through in places where something had cut deep enough to leave permanent wounds in the structure of reality.
Everything here pulsed with endings.

Noah could tell, with the clarity of a being whose Civilizations were steeped in this exact truth, that this Observable Existence was on a path toward destruction. Not threatened with it. On the path to it, the outcome already determined, the only remaining variable being how long the dying would take!
And yet, far ahead in this dying place, he saw a massive obsidian gold castle surrounded by towers.
The castle was full of life. Abundant life, abundant power, the vitality of an occupied stronghold standing in defiance of everything dying around it.
From the castle, an aura locked onto him and came over.
Sir William Arthur arrived before him, gazing at Noah with his composed neutrality, and then blinked in genuine surprise at the aura Noah was radiating.

He took a moment, focusing, the assessment of THE Aura of THE Source Barbarian and a faint expression of the Pure Primordial Essence that Noah hid visibly registering as something he had not expected to find. Then he set the surprise aside with the discipline of a man who set many things aside.

"One of the places to undergo trials to become a Sword of Existence," he said, "are Terminal Observable Existences. Domains that have had their Cause destroyed, and by extension, the Observable Existence itself placed on a path toward destruction. It is a failure of existence when this happens. It is a deeper failure when it happens by the hands of others rather than through natural collapse."
He gestured at the dying expanse around them, at the burning golden mountains and the torn dimensional fabric and the obsidian gold castle standing full of life in the middle of all of it.

sentences.text: He put on the suit.

The Lesser Existential Source Armament settled over him with the precision of something made to exact specification, the obsidian jacket finding his body, the white shirt beneath it, the obsidian tie sitting clean against the shirt.
He adjusted it without rushing, and the Source weaving in the composite recognized him the moment the last piece settled.
Taylor was still sitting on the grave she had dug.
"Wowee..." She shook her head slowly.
"You really had to do a whole power move of changing right in front of me like that?"
She said it like a complaint.
Her eyes said something else entirely, shining with the appreciation of someone who had seen a great many things across a long existence and was filing this one under things worth having seen!
Noah ignored her and reached for the blade.
THE Sovereign Reckoning came to his hand, the blue-obsidian sheath cool against his palm, and with the suit on and the blade in hand, the picture completed itself.
He looked grand!
Magisterial!

Obsidian tendrils of light began to swirl around the suit, rising from the Source weaving in slow deliberate spirals, and over all of it THE Aura of THE Source Barbarian glowed across his entire body, the obsidian gold of it running beneath and around the obsidian suit so that the two layers of obsidian, the worn and the innate, complemented rather than competed.
He floated above the golden sands.
"Persevere.
Exelissomai."
BOOM!

The multicolored flames and the obsidian gold surged around him simultaneously, the two Prime Letters expressing at once, and the flames spilled outward across THE Early Veiled Shore and beyond it into the vastness of THE Infiniverse, the domain receiving the effects the way she received everything he produced now.

He kept uttering them, every second, the way he had been uttering Persevere, the two Prime Letters refining and elevating his existence with each repetition, THE Aura of THE Source Barbarian growing fractionally more terrifying with every utterance because that was simply what it did now!
Below, Taylor clapped her hands together and whistled, low and appreciative.
The obsidian tendrils that had been forming around the suit since he put it on activated.

He watched them closely as they wove together into a bubble of obsidian light, the Source weaving carrying out exactly what Sir William had described it would do, and the body inside the bubble disappeared.
WAP!
Another of his bodies descended to THE Early Veiled Shore a moment later.
He had several to spare.
The distribution of his existence across domains meant that sending one off to a trial did not leave him absent from anywhere that mattered.
But the one inside the bubble began crossing the vastness of existence, pulled forward by the mechanism of the Source Armament.
Noah felt his existence being drawn across THE Undefined Gaps of existence,and once more, he left his Observable Existence entirely.
He knew what the Gaps were.
He had sent THE Infiniverse into them.
He described them as the unclassified regions between defined existence, the spaces of no definition where ordinary beings dissolved.

Experiencing them himself was a different thing from understanding them, and what he experienced was his existence being carried on unstable rivers of undefined potential, the terminal infinity within them pressing against his perception with a density that he could sense would have reduced Second Scale entities to paste through proximity alone.
The Source Armament handled it.

It had a set of directions encoded into its weaving, a destination it was pulling him toward, and it provided sufficient power and protection that he didn’t have to do anything but experience the journey.

He sensed the distant Undefined Weavings of existence moving around him, the raw uncategorized potential of the spaces between defined domains, the terminal infinity running through the obsidian rivers that carried him.
It was, he thought, a genuinely pleasant way to travel.

Surfing on obsidian rivers of terminal infinity in a well-cut suit with a Source Lifeform’s blade in hand, the most dangerous spaces in existence held at a comfortable distance by the armament’s protection.
After what felt like a few minutes, definition began to return.
He sensed it before he arrived in it, the definition of endings and catastrophe and apocalypses, obsidian gray light gathering around him as the Undefined Gaps released him into a defined domain.
And the moment the definition settled, his existence recognized what it was recognizing, because he carried many Civilizations related to endings and Apocalypse sat at the forefront of them.
He arrived in a place that was dying.
This Observable Existence stretched around him in the state of something that had been mortally wounded and had not yet finished the slow process of expiring.
Weavings of decaying folds drifted through the space, half-dissolved, the structures that should have held them together failing in slow motion.
Torn and destroyed Wheels of Existence hung in the distance, their architecture shattered, the cyclical mechanisms that governed the domain’s continuation broken past any repair he could see.
He felt like he was standing inside the shattered remnants of a Primordial Realm, the scale of the destruction vast enough that individual catastrophes blurred into a single condition.
Split golden mountains burned in the distance with roaring flames of terminal infinity, the fire consuming what it touched and producing nothing, the flame of endings rather than transformation.

Entire portions of the dimensional space carried tears that looked like glass-like cuts across existence itself, the fabric of the domain sliced through in places where something had cut deep enough to leave permanent wounds in the structure of reality.
Everything here pulsed with endings.
Noah could tell, with the clarity of a being whose Civilizations were steeped in this exact truth, that this Observable Existence was on a path toward destruction.
Not threatened with it.
On the path to it, the outcome already determined, the only remaining variable being how long the dying would take!
And yet, far ahead in this dying place, he saw a massive obsidian gold castle surrounded by towers.
The castle was full of life.
Abundant life, abundant power, the vitality of an occupied stronghold standing in defiance of everything dying around it.
From the castle, an aura locked onto him and came over.
Sir William Arthur arrived before him, gazing at Noah with his composed neutrality, and then blinked in genuine surprise at the aura Noah was radiating.

He took a moment, focusing, the assessment of THE Aura of THE Source Barbarian and a faint expression of the Pure Primordial Essence that Noah hid visibly registering as something he had not expected to find.
Then he set the surprise aside with the discipline of a man who set many things aside.
"One of the places to undergo trials to become a Sword of Existence," he said, "are Terminal Observable Existences.
Domains that have had their Cause destroyed, and by extension, the Observable Existence itself placed on a path toward destruction.
It is a failure of existence when this happens.
It is a deeper failure when it happens by the hands of others rather than through natural collapse."
He gestured at the dying expanse around them, at the burning golden mountains and the torn dimensional fabric and the obsidian gold castle standing full of life in the middle of all of it.
"Welcome to THE Terminal Observable Existence, Chernobyl."

chapters.title: Chapter 5314: Emotion I
paragraphs: "Come on, let me show you a few things."
Sir William rose, and Noah rose with him, and together they moved across the dying expanse of Chernobyl.
Anything apocalyptic and dying always had his full attention as he loved exploring new things!

The first region they crossed had been a place of war once. Noah could feel it in the residue, THE Bellum Cause of this Observable Existence still present in faint traces across the torn landscape, but the Cause was failing.

Where his own integrated Bellum Cause burned with the clean war-truth that conflict drove change, the Bellum Cause here flickered, its expression stuttering, the foundational truth it had once asserted no longer held steadily by the Observable Existence that had birthed it. Crimson light guttered across the ruined terrain like a flame running out of what fed it.

"A Cause...does not die quickly,"Sir William said as they passed over it. "This is the first thing the uninitiated misunderstand about the death of an Observable Existence. They imagine a sudden ending, a single catastrophic moment. The truth is slower and considerably crueler. A Cause that has lost its foundation continues asserting itself out of habit, the way a body continues twitching after the thing that animated it has gone. THE Bellum Cause of Chernobyl still tries to express the truth of conflict. It simply no longer has the foundation to express it correctly, so it produces only this. Flickering. The memory of war without the substance of it."
They moved on.

The next region had held knowledge. THE Cognitio Cause’s residue ran through it, libraries of folded information that had once organized the understanding of an entire Observable Existence now coming apart, the structured knowledge dissolving back into undifferentiated noise.
Noah watched vast archives of Cognitio expression unravel in slow motion, eons of accumulated understanding losing its organization and becoming meaningless.

"THE Cognitio Cause governed how this Observable Existence understood itself," Sir William said. "What you are watching is not the destruction of knowledge. It is something worse. It is knowledge forgetting how to be knowledge. The information remains. The capacity to organize it into understanding is what has failed. The beings who once lived here, in their final ages, could perceive everything and comprehend nothing, surrounded by the full record of their civilization and unable to read a word of it."

Noah said nothing. He filed each observation, building a picture of what the death of an Observable Existence actually looked like from the inside, because this was information his Civilizations of endings could use and because the dying around him was teaching him things no intact domain ever could.
A man could always continue learning!

They passed regions where other Causes failed in their own ways. A Cause of growth that produced only decay. A Cause of binding that could no longer hold anything together. Each one a foundational truth that had lost its foundation, each one continuing to try and continuing to fail,the whole Observable Existence a collection of broken promises that existence was still attempting to keep out of momentum alone.
"You are wondering how this happened," Sir William said.

Noah was. He had been since he arrived. An Observable Existence did not simply have its First Cause undone. THE First Cause was the foundational axiom the entire domain was built around. Undoing it required something that Noah’s understanding of existence did not readily account for.
Sir William slowed as they approached the torn dimensional fabric near the burning golden mountains, the glass-like cuts across reality catching the terminal infinity’s light.

"Then I will tell you of The Records of Chernobyl," he said."It is worth knowing. The Swords of Existence use it as instruction, because it teaches the single lesson that matters most about the beings we exist to oppose."
He floated, and he spoke, and his measured cadence filled the dying air.

"In the ages when Chernobyl lived, it was a domain of considerable abundance. Its First Cause was strong. Its Causes expressed cleanly. The Lifeforms within it climbed and flourished and produced civilizations worth remembering. And among the beings who reached the highest tiers of this Observable Existence, two fell in love.

One was an Infinite Lifeform. A being of this domain who had cultivated Infinity to a height few ever reached. The other was a Source Lifeform, ancient and powerful, carrying THE Primordial Source in the direct way that Source Lifeforms carry it.

Their love was, by every account that survived, genuine. It was not a strategic alliance dressed as affection. It was not a transaction. Two beings of immense power found in each other something that the immensity of their power had never been able to provide on its own, and they chose each other, across the difference in their natures, against the considerable pressures that such a difference produced."
Noah listened.

"Love between beings of that tier is rare," Sir William continued. "Beings who climb to such heights tend to lose, somewhere in the climbing, the capacity for it. Power and intimacy are not natural companions. That these two retained both was, in its way, an achievement greater than the power itself. They did not harm anyone. They did not threaten the order of their Observable Existence. They simply loved each other, two beings of different natures, in a domain large enough to hold them both."
He paused, and the pause carried the weight of someone arriving at the part of the story that mattered.
"There was a third. Another Infinite Lifeform, of comparable tier to the first. And this being looked at the love between the Infinite Lifeform and the Source Lifeform and saw an abomination.

The reasons matter less than you would think. Perhaps the third loved the first and could not bear to be unchosen. Perhaps the third held convictions about the separation of natures that the love offended. Perhaps it was simply the specific rage of a powerful being who encountered something it disapproved of and could not tolerate the existence of a thing it disapproved of. The chronicles disagree on the reason. They agree entirely on the result."
The burning golden mountains roared in the distance.

"The third Infinite Lifeform moved against the lovers. And the lovers, being who they were, did not simply submit. What followed was... a war between three beings of the highest tiers an Observable Existence had ever produced, and a war at that tier is not contained by the participants. It spread. It pulled in allies and forced choices on beings who wanted no part of it. The Source Lifeform’s nature drew responses from across existence. The Infinite Lifeforms’ war tore at the foundations of the domain that held them.

And in the height of it, when the three of them brought everything they were against each other with no remaining restraint, they struck at THE First Cause itself. Whether by intention or by the simple inability of a domain to contain that magnitude of conflict, THE First Cause of Chernobyl was wounded. And a wounded First Cause, unlike a wounded being, cannot heal. It can only unravel.

The lovers died. The third died. And the Observable Existence they had fought within received its death sentence in the same moment, the First Cause beginning the slow unraveling that you see around you now, the Causes failing one by one, the domain forgetting how to be a domain, the whole of Chernobyl placed on the path toward an ending that no being remaining within it had the power to prevent."
BOOM!

chapters.title: Chapter 5315: Emotion II
paragraphs: He turned to Noah.

"Countless Lifeforms lived here. They had no part in the love, or the disapproval, or the war. They were simply present in an Observable Existence whose most powerful beings could not control their emotions, and that was sufficient to end them.

The lovers were not villains. The third was not, in its own understanding, a villain either. None of them set out to destroy an Observable Existence. They were simply beings who held great power and could not govern what they felt, and at their tier, the inability to govern what you feel is not a personal failing.It is an extinction event."
The terminal infinity burned across the dying expanse.
"This is the lesson the Swords of Existence take from Chernobyl,"Sir William said.

"It is not that love is dangerous, though small minds draw that conclusion. It is not that difference must be policed, though crueler minds draw that one. The lesson is simpler and harder.Power without the governance of one’s own emotions is the single greatest threat existence contains."

"Not malice. Malice is rare and can be planned around. The thing that ends Observable Existences is ordinary feeling, love and disapproval and rage and grief, carried by beings powerful enough that their ordinary feelings reshape reality."
He looked at the dying domain around them, at the failing Causes and the torn fabric and the abundant life still burning in the obsidian gold castle that defied all of it.

"You will be tested here,"he said. "Among the ruins of beings who could not govern themselves. I find it appropriate.A Sword of Existence who cannot govern their own feeling is not a Sword. It is the next Chernobyl, waiting for a reason."
He began to move toward the castle.
"Come. The trial does not begin until you understand what it is held among. Now you understand, we shall proceed"
HUUM!
"Every trial to select a new Sword of Existence is overseen by at least three current Swords,"Sir William said as they moved.
He spoke without looking at Noah, his attention forward, the dying expanse of Chernobyl unrolling beneath them as they traveled toward something Noah could already feel before he could see it.

"Everything happening here is observed. How you approach what is put in front of you, how you reason through it, what you choose when the choice has no comfortable answer, all of it is being watched and weighed by beings who have walked this path themselves and have no patience for those who walk it poorly." He paused.

"I tell you this not to unsettle you. I tell you because a Sword operates under observation for the rest of their existence, accountable to THE Source and to the others who serve it, and a being who cannot function under observation has no business holding the designation. Consider it the first thing the trial measures, before the trial itself begins."
They flew on.

"The first trial is simple," Sir William continued. "Simple in the way that the most important things are simple. It will not test your power. Your power has already been assessed and found sufficient, or you would not be here. It will test something the powerful almost never develop, because their power lets them avoid developing it."
They arrived.

The region was where the storms of unstable First Cause raged strongest in all of Chernobyl. Definition and Undefinition warred against each other across the space in churning fronts, the boundaries between what existed and what did not existing nowhere consistently, terminal infinity running through all of it in obsidian gray currents that pulsed with the weight of endings.

Reality here was not torn the way it was torn elsewhere in the domain. It was actively coming apart and being held together in the same moment, the two processes locked in a contest that neither was winning.
At the center of the contest, far below, something held the whole thing together.
"Below you," Sir William said, "isone of the last remaining Infinite Lifeforms of this Observable Existence."
Noah looked down.

"She was very young when THE First Cause was destroyed. A child, by the reckoning of beings of her tier. In the catastrophe, as the First Cause began its unraveling, she did something that no one instructed her to do and that no one has been able to undo since. She latched onto it. Her infinite existence became a battery, a living anchor, holding THE Mortis Cause intact when it should have failed with all the others."
Sir William’s voice carried the somber weight he reserved for the things that genuinely moved him.

"THE Mortis Cause governs endings. By holding it intact, she has held off the ending of this entire Observable Existence. THE First Cause should have finished unraveling eons ago. The decillions who still survive in this domain, including everyone in the castle behind us, should have perished long since. They have not, because a child latched onto THE Mortis Cause and refused to let go, and has been holding the ending of an entire Observable Existence away from everyone within it ever since."
Noah was beginning to understand where this was going.

"Because she holds the endings," Sir William said, "she experiences them. Every moment. The agony of Mortis for an entire Observable Existence, channeled through a single infinite existence that was a child when it took the weight on and has been a child carrying it ever since. The pain is constant. It does not diminish. It is the suffering of every ending she holds at bay, felt all at once, every moment, for longer than most beings could imagine enduring it."
He looked down at her.

"As of yesterday, she could no longer bear it. She has begun to wail. To beg to be released from it. The endings have become too much even for a being born of Infinity, and she wants it to stop. She wants out."
The weight of it settled.

"But ending her is the problem," Sir William said. "She is the last anchor holding THE Mortis Cause together. The moment she is released, THE Mortis Cause fails. The moment THE Mortis Cause fails, THE First Cause finishes its unraveling, and every remaining decillion in this Observable Existence perishes as the final thread holding all the Causes together gives way. Her suffering is the only thing keeping countless lives in existence. Her release is the only thing that will end her suffering. Those are the two truths, and they cannot both be honored."
He turned to Noah.
"A Sword of Existence was assigned to address this. It is not their task anymore. It is yours."His eyes held Noah’s. "What will you do?"

"What will you do?"

chapters.title: Chapter 5316: Emotion III
paragraphs: Noah looked down through the rivers of terminal infinity.
Past the obsidian gray currents and the warring fronts of definition and Undefinition, he saw her.

A little girl, no older than ten by any human reckoning, curled in a fetal position and spinning slowly in the storm of unstable First Cause that she herself was holding together. Her face was visible in glimpses as she turned. It showed pain. Not discomfort, not distress, but the specific excruciating agony of a being experiencing more suffering than any frame was built to hold, held at a pitch that did not waver because the thing producing it did not waver.
She was small. She wore tattered blue rags that had once been garments of Infinity, the fabric carrying faint traces of what it had been before eons of holding endings wore it down to threads.

Her hair drifted around her in the currents. She looked, in the glimpses Noah caught of her face, like something that should have been protected by everything around it and had instead been asked to protect everything around it.
And she had said yes, because she had been too young to understand what saying yes would cost.
She turned in the storm and her eyes found him.

She looked at him pitifully, the gaze of a child who had been in pain for longer than she could remember, who saw a new presence and felt, beneath the agony, the faint flicker of a hope she had probably learned not to trust. So young. So innocent.
Bearing the endings of an entire Observable Existence in every moment, and looking at him with eyes that asked, without words, whether he was someone who could make it stop.
|Infinite Lifeform — Status assessment.|
|Designation: Seo-yeon. Infinite Lifeform of THE Observable Existence of Chernobyl.|

|Apparent age at First Cause destruction: equivalent to ten years. Actual duration of existence since: incalculable through standard measurement. She has existed in a held state, neither aging nor developing, since the catastrophe.|
|Current function: Living anchor for THE Mortis Cause. Her infinite existence is the sole structure preventing THE Mortis Cause from failing and THE First Cause from completing its unraveling.|

|Current condition: Sustained maximal agony. She is channeling the endings of an entire Observable Existence through her singular existence continuously. The suffering has no intervals. As of recent, her capacity to endure has been exceeded and she is actively seeking release. She seeks death.|
|Dependent population: Incalculable. All remaining life in THE Observable Existence of Chernobyl persists solely because of her continued function.|

|Resolution available through standard means: None. Her release ends her suffering and ends the dependent population. Her continuation preserves the dependent population and continues her suffering. There is no apparent third option.|
Noah gazed at her.
Far above, in a space held apart from the dying domain and surrounded by THE Primordial Source, another body of Sir William stood observing.

Three Source Lifeforms stood beside him, each of a different lineage, each carrying THE Primordial Source in a distinct expression that marked them as products of separate origins across the vastness of existence.
They watched the region below where Noah hung above the storm, gauging, weighing, the three current Swords of Existence who would render the verdict on whether the trial had been passed.
One of them spoke.

"Why," the Source Lifeform said, its voice carrying the genuine curiosity of a being asking a question it found legitimately puzzling, "is a task meant for a full Sword of Existence being given to a Trial Sword? This is not a trial assignment. This is a working assignment that a seated Sword should have closed." It looked at Sir William.
"Do you want your pick to fail? Have you tired of sponsorship? Because handing a Trial Sword a problem that has no clean solution is not how one shepherds a candidate toward success."
Sir William watched the region below with composed attention.

"I am no longer interested in sponsoring those who have it easy," he said. "I have done that. I have shepherded capable beings through trials calibrated to let them pass, and I have produced competent Swords who handle competent assignments competently, and existence has gained from them what existence gains from competence. It was not nothing. It was also not what I am looking for now."
He continued watching Noah.

"Hardship and adversity breed wonder. This is not sentiment. It is the single most reliable principle I have observed across the full length of my existence. The exceptional are not produced by trials they were meant to pass. They are produced by the moments where there was no clean answer and they found something anyway, where the situation offered only bad options and they refused to accept that the list of options was complete."

His voice carried the weight of conviction settled over a very long time. "I am only looking for that which is truly exceptional now. I have grown too old and seen too much to spend my sponsorship on anything less. If he is what I suspect he is, this trial will not break him. It will reveal him. And if I am wrong, then I have learned something useful about the limits of what radiates from him, and I will have lost nothing but time, of which I have a great deal."
The Source Lifeform considered this.
"And if he simply chooses one of the two answers? Releases the child, or preserves the population and leaves her to suffer? Both are defensible. Both are what most would choose."

"Then he is competent," Sir William said. "And competent is not what I am sponsoring anymore. Existence is vast and filled with terrors, and it needs more than competent Swords. We have seen competent Sword and even ourselves...can be considered competent. What is needed in these times is something unfathomably more. But...let us see. Let us see."
Below, Noah continued to gaze at the little girl spinning in the storm of endings she had been holding back since before she should have understood what holding them back would cost her!
